structure.summary:
- Signatures
  - Formal sign-off of the report pursuant to the Securities Exchange Act of 1934.
  - Executed by American Express Company officers and directors, including Chairman/CEO Stephen J. Squeri and Vice Chairman/CFO Jeffrey C. Campbell; dated February 10, 2023.

- Appendix: Statistical Disclosure by Bank Holding Companies
  - Purpose and scope: Supplemental bank holding company data to be read with MD&A and Consolidated Financial Statements.
  - Distribution of assets, liabilities, and shareholders’ equity; interest rates and interest differential:
    - Three-year average balance sheets (2022, 2021, 2020) detailing major interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities, split between U.S. and non-U.S. offices.
    - Interest income, interest expense, and average yields/rates across categories (deposits in other banks, securities, Card Member loans and receivables, other loans).
    - Key 2022 metrics: total average interest-earning assets $128.4B; net interest income $9.9B; net interest yield 7.7% (interest rate spread 7.9%).
    - Notable trends/drivers: higher yields on deposits and loans; increased card loan volumes; higher deposit and long-term debt costs as rates rose.
    - Footnotes on methodology (month-end averaging, inclusion of non-accrual loans, tax-equivalent yields, and fair value exclusions).
  - Non-interest-earning assets and liabilities:
    - Breakouts of cash, receivables, reserves for credit losses, and other assets by geography.
    - Total average assets $205.5B in 2022; non-U.S. share of average assets 20.4%; non-U.S. share of average liabilities 9.0%.
  - Interest-bearing and non-interest-bearing liabilities:
    - Detail on customer deposits (savings, time, demand), short-term borrowings, long-term debt, and other liabilities by geography.
  - Volume and rate analysis:
    - Attribution of changes in net interest income to average volume vs. average rate movements (e.g., card loan growth and rate increases were primary positives; deposit and debt rate increases raised interest expense).
  - Investment securities yields and maturities:
    - Weighted average yields by contractual maturity bucket for available-for-sale debt securities as of year-end 2022 (state/municipal, U.S. Treasury/agency, MBS, foreign government, other).
  - Maturities and interest-rate sensitivity:
    - Contractual maturity schedule for loans and Card Member receivables by customer type (consumer, small business, corporate, other).
    - Identification of fixed vs. variable-rate composition for loans due after one year; notes that card loans and receivables have no stated maturity and that longer-dated balances reflect TDRs.
  - Credit quality indicators:
    - Net write-offs and write-off rates for consumer, small business, and other loans; and for consumer, small business, and corporate receivables (2022 vs. 2021).
    - Reserve for credit losses ($4.0B at 2022 YE), non-accrual loans, and related ratios.
  - Allocation of reserve for credit losses:
    - Breakdown among Card Member loans (majority), Card Member receivables, and other loans.
  - Uninsured time certificates of deposit:
    - Amounts by remaining maturity and by U.S./non-U.S. offices; FDIC insurance context.

- Exhibit 10.1: Deferred Compensation Plan for Directors and Advisors (amended and restated effective January 1, 2023)
  - Eligibility: Non-employee Directors and Advisors of American Express Company and American Express National Bank.
  - Administration: Nominating and Governance Committee; authority may be delegated to the Corporate Secretary.
  - Deferral elections: Directors may defer 50% or 100% of Board/committee compensation; timing rules for initial and ongoing elections; Section 409A compliance.
  - Account structure: Pre-2015 and annual “Class Year Accounts”; quarterly crediting (or at Payment Event Date if applicable).
  - Investment options:
    - AFR-Based Option: interest credited at 120% of the applicable federal long-term rate (compounded; valued through Payment Event Date).
    - Share Equivalent Option: amounts converted into share equivalent units (SEUs) of AXP common stock; dividend equivalents; anti-dilution adjustments; valuation based on 15-day average price prior to Payment Event Date.
    - Post-separation changes to investment options may be permitted by the Administrator.
  - SEU Award Accounts: SEUs awarded under the separate 2003 SEU Plan are credited to Class Year SEU Award Accounts and treated like SEUs under the Share Equivalent Option.
  - Payment elections:
    - Timing: upon separation from service or a specified anniversary up to the 10th anniversary thereafter; default is lump sum upon separation if no election.
    - Form: lump sum or up to 10 annual installments.
    - Changes to elections: permitted with 12-month waiting period and at least 5-year deferral from original payment date; must still be paid by the 10th anniversary of separation.
  - Death: lump-sum payment to estate or designated beneficiaries.
  - General provisions: payments within 90 days of Payment Event Date; unfunded and unsecured obligations; statements of account; amendment limits; plan termination rules; explicit Section 409A compliance.

- Exhibit 10.20: Twelfth Amendment and Restatement of the American Express Retirement Restoration Plan (effective January 1, 2023)
  - Scope: Nonqualified “top-hat” plan (ERISA) for a select group of management/highly compensated employees; formerly the Supplemental Retirement Plan.
  - Content overview (per table of contents and excerpts):
    - History and effective dates detailing plan evolution since 1973, multiple amendments, and coordination with qualified plans (Retirement Plan “RP” and Retirement Savings Plan “RSP”).
    - Definitions; administration and authority.
    - Eligibility and participation.
    - Supplemental benefits:
      - Restoration of benefits limited under qualified plans (e.g., benefits in excess of Code limits), including RP-related and RSP-related components; company matching/profit-sharing make-whole features; account crediting rules and participant elections.
    - Elective deferrals:
      - Deferrable compensation types, participation windows (including newly eligible employees), deferral elections, and crediting mechanics.
    - Earnings crediting:
      - Hypothetical investment methods and interest methods; restrictions and options for crediting returns to accounts.
    - Payment of benefits:
      - Distribution timing and forms for supplemental and deferral accounts; beneficiary designations; payments on death, disability, unforeseeable emergency; de minimis cash-out; tax withholding; company offset.
    - Change in control:
      - Definitions and effects on accounts/crediting (e.g., special earnings crediting rules).
    - Claims procedures and arbitration framework.
    - Amendment and termination provisions.
    - General provisions: unfunded status; non-transferability; no employment rights; Section 409A compliance; governing law.
  - Transition/grandfathering:
    - Treatment of pre-2005 “grandfathered” supplemental and deferral benefits under prior plans; loss of grandfathered status for certain benefits; consolidation and administration under current plan terms consistent with Section 409A.

nodes.title: Effective Date
nodes.heading: Section 1.2 Effective Date .
nodes.start_phrase: Except as expressl y provided otherwise herein, the Plan as amended and restated hereby is generally effective January 1, 2023, provided that provisions which are clarifying in nature reflect the intended interpretation of pre- existing plan terms and are ef fective as of the date that the relevant original provision was added to the Plan.
nodes.summary:
- States compliance with ERISA and DOL Regulation 2520.104-23.
- Establishes the effective date of the amended and restated Plan as January 1, 2023, with clarifying provisions applied retroactively to the dates original terms were added.
- Provides transition rules:
  - Supplemental Benefits: Benefits accrued under the Prior SRP Plan as of December 31, 2004 are treated as “Grandfathered Supplemental Benefits,” administered under the Prior SRP Plan in accordance with Code Section 409A and Notice 2005-1; participant elections cannot materially modify prior rights.
  - Deferral Benefits: For plan years through 2007, deferrals were under the “Prior Deferral Plan” (including the American Express Salary Deferral Plan, Pay-for-Performance Deferral Programs, and similar nonqualified deferral plans); for plan years beginning 2008, deferrals are under this Plan.
  - Grandfathered Deferral Benefits: Deferrals earned and vested before January 1, 2005 remained under the Prior Deferral Plan; effective October 27, 2010, earnings credits on such amounts are administered under Article 7 of this Plan; in a Change in Control, additional earnings credits due under the Prior Deferral Plan are credited at the AFR.
  - All other benefits are governed solely by this Plan, as amended; effective January 1, 2011, “Formerly Grandfathered Deferral Benefits” lost their grandfathered status and were distributed per Section 1.4; any remaining Grandfathered Deferral Benefits (including those attributable to Degrandfathered Participants) continue to be subject to the Prior Deferral Plan.
- Allows an Appendix to summarize the form and timing of payments for Grandfathered Supplemental Benefits, Grandfathered Deferral Benefits, and Formerly Grandfathered Deferral Benefits for reference only, without changing those terms.
- Begins Section 1.4 on modification of certain grandfathered benefits, effective January 1, 2011, for Degrandfathered Participants whose Formerly Grandfathered Deferral Benefits were not scheduled to begin by year-end (text truncated).

nodes.title: Transition Rules
nodes.heading: Section 1.3 Transition Rules .
nodes.start_phrase: Each Participant’ s accrued benefit under the Prior SRP Plan as of December 31, 2004 (“Grandfathered Supplemental Benefits ”) was determined by the Administrator in accordance with Section 409A of the Code and Notice 2005-1.
nodes.summary:
- Identifies the plan as an ERISA-covered, nonqualified arrangement administered under DOL Regulation 2520.104-23.
- States the amended and restated plan’s general effective date as January 1, 2023, with clarifying provisions retroactive to the dates the original terms were added.
- Establishes transition rules distinguishing:
  - Grandfathered Supplemental Benefits (accrued as of December 31, 2004) determined under Code Section 409A and Notice 2005-1, administered under the Prior SRP Plan; participant elections cannot materially modify that plan.
  - Deferral Benefits provided under prior nonqualified deferral programs through December 31, 2007 (the “Prior Deferral Plan”) and under this Plan beginning January 1, 2008.
  - Grandfathered Deferral Benefits (earned and vested before January 1, 2005) that remain subject to the Prior Deferral Plan; as of October 27, 2010, earnings credits on these amounts are administered per Article 7 of this Plan.
  - Change in Control treatment where additional earnings credits due under the Prior Deferral Plan are credited at the AFR.
  - Effective January 1, 2011, certain amounts (“Formerly Grandfathered Deferral Benefits”) lost their grandfathered status and were to be distributed under Section 1.4; remaining grandfathered amounts continue under the Prior Deferral Plan.
- Allows an Appendix, updatable by the Administrator, to summarize the form and timing of payments for grandfathered and formerly grandfathered benefits, without altering those terms.
- Introduces Section 1.4, which modifies certain grandfathered benefits effective January 1, 2011 for Degrandfathered Participants whose benefits were not yet in pay status (details continue beyond the excerpt).

nodes.title: Modification of Certain Grandfathered Benefits
nodes.heading: Section 1.4 Modification of Certain Grandfather ed Benefits .
nodes.start_phrase: Effective January 1, 2011, the Formerly Grandfathered Deferral Benefits of each Degrandfathered Participant which are not scheduled to be in pay status by December 31, 2016 shall be payable in a lump sum on March 1, 2012 unless otherwise elected pursuant to Section 1.4(b).
nodes.summary:
- Establishes that the plan is governed by ERISA and related DOL regulations, and references compliance with Code Section 409A and IRS Notice 2005-1.
- Sets the effective date of the amended and restated plan as January 1, 2023, with clarifying provisions applied retroactively to original intent.
- Provides transition rules for legacy benefits:
  - Grandfathered Supplemental Benefits (accrued under the Prior SRP Plan as of December 31, 2004) remain under the Prior SRP Plan and cannot be materially modified.
  - Deferral Benefits were provided under prior nonqualified deferral plans through 2007; this Plan governs from 2008 forward.
  - Pre-2005 Grandfathered Deferral Benefits remain under the Prior Deferral Plan; from October 27, 2010, their earnings credits follow Article 7 of this Plan.
  - In a Change in Control, additional earnings under the Prior Deferral Plan are credited at the AFR.
  - Effective January 1, 2011, certain Formerly Grandfathered Deferral Benefits lost grandfathered status and were distributed per Section 1.4; remaining grandfathered benefits continue under the Prior Deferral Plan.
  - An Appendix may summarize payment form/timing for grandfathered benefits for reference without altering those terms.
- Modifies certain grandfathered benefits (Section 1.4):
  - Effective January 1, 2011, Formerly Grandfathered Deferral Benefits not in pay status by December 31, 2016 are paid in a lump sum on March 1, 2012 unless a timely alternate election was made.
  - Earnings on these amounts are credited under the Interest Credit Method through December 31, 2011; for Executive Officers, credits are capped at the AFR (with limited exceptions); earnings for early 2012 are at the AFR.
  - By December 31, 2010, participants could elect lump sum or 5/10/15 annual installments, payable on a specified date no earlier than July 1, 2017 or at Retirement (no earlier than July 1, 2017), with specific timing rules upon Separation from Service and 90-day administrative payment windows.
  - Death before completion of payments is handled under Section 8.4 for Post-2010 Deferral Benefits.
  - Such elections become effective January 1, 2012; if payment was delayed, credits remain under the Interest Credit Method through 2011, then switch to the Hypothetical Investment Method as of January 1, 2012; AFR cap for Executive Officers applies.
- Begins Article 2 (Definitions) and defines “Account” as the combination of a Participant’s Deferral Account and Supplemental Account.

nodes.title: DEFINITIONS
nodes.heading: ARTICLE 2 DEFINITIONS
nodes.start_phrase: As used in the Plan, the following terms have the meanings indicated below:
nodes.summary:
- Sets default payout for Formerly Grandfathered Deferral Benefits in a lump sum on March 1, 2012 unless an alternative election under Section 1.4(b) was made.
- Specifies earnings crediting for amounts scheduled for March 1, 2012: Interest Credit Method through December 31, 2011; for the portion of 2012 before payment, earnings credited at the AFR; if a Participant becomes an Executive Officer, earnings on Formerly Grandfathered amounts are capped at the AFR (except amounts already paid above AFR before becoming an Executive Officer).
- Allows Degrandfathered Participants, by December 31, 2010, to elect lump sum or 5/10/15 annual installments payable on a specified January 1 or July 1 no earlier than July 1, 2017 (or upon Retirement, but not earlier than July 1, 2017), with subsequent installments each January 1 or July 1 and up to 90 days administrative processing.
- If a Separation from Service occurs before the elected specified date, payments begin on the later of July 1, 2017 or the January 1/July 1 at least six months after separation; for installment elections, payments commence the later of July 1, 2017 or July 1 of the calendar year following the year of separation, then continue each July 1, subject to up to 90 days administrative processing.
- If a Participant dies before payments are complete, remaining payments follow Section 8.4 rules applicable to Post-2010 Deferral Benefits.
- Any subsequent election mentioned becomes effective January 1, 2012.
- For Degrandfathered Participants who elect to delay payment, Formerly Grandfathered amounts earn under the Interest Credit Method through December 31, 2011 (subject to AFR cap for Executive Officers), then shift to the Hypothetical Investment Method as of January 1, 2012.
- Begins Article 2 (Definitions) and defines “Account” as the Participant’s Deferral Account and Supplemental Account collectively.

nodes.title: Definitions
nodes.heading: Section 2.1 Definitions .
nodes.start_phrase: As used in the Plan, the following terms have the meanings indicated below:
nodes.summary:
- Payment and earnings rules for Formerly Grandfathered/Degrandfathered Deferral Benefits:
  - Amounts scheduled for March 1, 2012 payout receive Interest Credit Method earnings through December 31, 2011; any period in 2012 before payment earns at AFR.
  - If a participant becomes an Executive Officer, credited earnings on Formerly Grandfathered amounts are capped at AFR (except amounts already paid above AFR before that status change).
  - By December 31, 2010, Degrandfathered Participants could elect lump sum or 5/10/15 annual installments, payable on a specified Jan 1 or Jul 1 no earlier than July 1, 2017, or upon Retirement (not earlier than July 1, 2017).
  - If Separation from Service occurs before the selected date, payment begins the later of July 1, 2017 or at least six months after separation; installment payments start the later of July 1, 2017 or July 1 of the year after separation and continue each July 1.
  - Death before completion is handled per Section 8.4 (Post-2010 Deferral Benefits rules).
  - Any subsequent election becomes effective January 1, 2012.
  - If payment is delayed by election, earnings continue under the Interest Credit Method through December 31, 2011 (subject to AFR cap for Executive Officers), then switch to the Hypothetical Investment Method as of January 1, 2012.

- Article 2: Key plan definitions and governance:
  - Core plan entities and roles: Administrator (Employee Benefits Administration Committee), Committee (Compensation and Benefits Committee), Investment Committee, Company (Amex and certain affiliates).
  - Accounts and benefits: Deferral Account, Supplemental Account (RP-Related and RSP-Related), Deferral Benefits, Supplemental Benefits, Supplemental Distributions, and related elections.
  - Participant categories and status: Participant, Employee, Executive Officer (Band 99), Non-Executive Officer, Degrandfathered Participant, Retiree, Retirement, Retirement Eligible, Former GE Employees.
  - Compensation and pay bases: Base Salary, Incentive Pay, and references to Total Pay; exclusions to prevent duplication with non-qualified deferrals.
  - Timing constructs: Plan Year (separate definitions for Supplemental vs. Deferral Benefits), Band 50 Determination Date, Deferral Benefits Eligibility Date.
  - Pre-/Post-2010 distinctions: Post-2010 and Pre-2011 Deferral Benefits; Formerly Grandfathered Deferral Benefits becoming subject to this Plan as of January 1, 2011.
  - Credit/economic measures: AFR (120% applicable federal long-term rate), Schedule Rate, Minimum Schedule Rate, Moody’s A Rate, Stock Fund.
  - Legal and compliance references: Code, Section 409A (and policy), Section 401(a)(17) compensation limits, Section 415 limitations, Exchange Act Section 16(a) (Insiders), Employment Arbitration Policy, Severance Plan references, Trust (grantor trust).
  - Events and conditions: Separation from Service, Disability (per 409A), Unforeseeable Emergency, Beneficiary.
  - Cross-references and interpretation: Undefined terms follow Qualified Retirement Plan meanings; grammatical rules for gender/number.

nodes.title: Qualified Plan Definitions
nodes.heading: Section 2.2 Quali fied Plan Definitions .
nodes.start_phrase: Capitalized terms not otherwise defined in the Plan shall have the same meaning set forth in the related Qualified Retirement Plan, to the extent applicable, as the context may imply .
nodes.summary:
- Defines key terms for an American Express supplemental retirement/deferred compensation plan, with heavy reliance on Internal Revenue Code Section 409A.
- “Separation from Service” is determined under Section 409A and the company’s Section 409A Policy.
- “Severance Plan” collectively references three Amex plans (Senior Executive Severance Plan, Severance Pay Plan, and Supplemental Unemployment Benefit Plan) and any successors.
- Establishes meanings for “Stock Fund” (the RSP Stock Fund), “Supplemental Account” (combining RP-Related and RSP-Related Accounts), “Supplemental Benefits,” “Supplemental Distribution,” and “Supplemental Election” (including automatic elections under Section 5.4).
- Describes the “Trust” created under Section 9.2(a) and intended to qualify as a grantor trust for federal tax purposes.
- Defines “Unforeseeable Emergency” in line with Section 409A (illness/accident, casualty loss, or other extraordinary, unforeseeable events beyond the participant’s control), as determined by the Administrator.
- Interpretation provisions: capitalized terms not defined adopt meanings from the related Qualified Retirement Plan (Section 2.2); pronoun, gender, and number usage rules clarify masculine/feminine/neuter and singular/plural (Section 2.3).

nodes.title: Gender and Number
nodes.heading: Section 2.3 Gender and Number .
nodes.start_phrase: All pronouns and any variations there of shall be deemed to refer to the masculine, feminine, or neuter , as the identity of the person or persons may require.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes key definitions central to a nonqualified “top-hat” deferred compensation plan, including:
  - Separation from Service aligned with Section 409A and the plan’s 409A Policy.
  - Severance Plan encompassing three specified American Express severance programs and their successors.
  - Stock Fund (the RSP Stock Fund).
  - Supplemental Account, Supplemental Benefits, Supplemental Distribution, and Supplemental Election (including Company-made Automatic New Participant Supplemental Elections under Section 5.4).
  - Trust structured as a grantor (rabbi) trust under the Internal Revenue Code.
  - Unforeseeable Emergency standard consistent with Section 409A (illness/accident, casualty loss, or similar extraordinary circumstances), determined by the Administrator.

- Interpretation and construction provisions:
  - Terms not defined in the plan adopt meanings from related Qualified Retirement Plans (Section 2.2).
  - Gender and number usage rules for consistent interpretation (Section 2.3).

- Administration framework (Article 3):
  - Identifies the Administrator and grants broad discretionary authority to interpret, construe, and administer the plan.
  - Empowers correction of defects, omissions, inconsistencies, and mathematical or accounting errors via equitable adjustments.
  - Administrator decisions are final, conclusive, and binding; authority may be delegated.
  - Notes Committee-related limitations by cross-reference to Section 10.7.

- Eligibility and participation (Article 4):
  - Participation limited to select Employees to maintain ERISA “top-hat” status; eligibility generally automatic for those who qualify, with the Administrator able to exclude individuals or categories.
  - Default eligibility threshold of Band 35 or above unless the Administrator determines otherwise.
  - Must also be a participant in a Company Qualified Retirement Plan.
  - For each Plan Year, eligibility requires either (i) an existing Account from a prior year (including those deemed to have an Account if they previously declined an offer), or (ii) Total Pay exceeding the Section 401(a)(17) compensation limit under the RSP definition.

nodes.title: ADMINISTRATION
nodes.heading: ARTICLE 3 ADMINISTRA TION
nodes.start_phrase: The Plan shall be administered by the Administrator .
nodes.summary:
- Article 3 (Administration): Establishes that the Plan is administered by an Administrator with broad authority to interpret, construe, and operate the Plan. The Administrator may correct defects, omissions, inconsistencies, and mathematical/accounting errors via equitable adjustments. Its decisions are final, conclusive, and binding on all Participants and Beneficiaries. The Administrator may delegate its authority and responsibilities, and such delegates are treated as the Administrator to the extent of delegation. The Administrator’s authority is subject to any limitations imposed by the Committee under Section 10.7.

- Article 4 (Eligibility): Limits participation to Employees meeting specified criteria and consistent with maintaining the Plan as an ERISA “top-hat” plan. Eligible Employees are generally those in Band 35 or above, though the Administrator may designate individuals or categories as ineligible. Participation is automatic for eligible Employees. To participate, an Employee must: (a) be a participant in a Company-maintained Qualified Retirement Plan; and (b) for the relevant Plan Year, either (i) have (or be deemed to have had, if a prior offer was declined) an Account from a prior Plan Year, or (ii) receive Total Pay (as defined under the RSP, ignoring the Section 401(a)(17) Limitation) in excess of the Section 401(a)(17) Limitation.

nodes.title: Administrator
nodes.heading: Section 3.1 Administrator .
nodes.start_phrase: The Plan shall be administered by the Administrator .
nodes.summary:
- Article 3 (Administration):
  - The Plan is administered by an Administrator.
  - The Administrator has broad authority to interpret, construe, and administer the Plan; correct defects, omissions, inconsistencies, and mathematical/accounting errors through equitable adjustments.
  - Decisions are final, conclusive, and binding on all Participants and Beneficiaries.
  - The Administrator may delegate authority and responsibilities; references to the Administrator include delegates to the extent of delegation.
  - The Administrator’s authority operates except as otherwise provided by the Committee and subject to limitations in Section 10.7.

- Article 4 (Eligibility):
  - Participation is limited to Employees meeting Section 4.2 and occurs automatically for those Employees.
  - The Administrator may exclude specific Employees or categories from all or parts of the Plan.
  - Eligibility must be consistent with the Plan’s status as a “top-hat” plan under ERISA.
  - Unless determined otherwise, Employees must be in Band 35 or above to be eligible.

- Section 4.2 (Participation requirements):
  - Employee must satisfy Section 4.1 and be a participant in a Company-maintained Qualified Retirement Plan (per that plan’s eligibility rules).
  - For the relevant Plan Year, the Employee must either:
    - Have an Account from a prior Plan Year (including being treated as having one if the Employee declined a prior participation offer), or
    - Receive Total Pay (as defined under the RSP, disregarding the Section 401(a)(17) limitation) exceeding the Section 401(a)(17) limit.

nodes.title: Authority
nodes.heading: Section 3.2 Authority .
nodes.start_phrase: Except as otherwise provided by the Committee (subject to the limitation on the Committee’ s authority under Section 10.7), the Admi nistrator shall have full power , authority and discretion to interpret, construe and administer the Plan, and such interpretation and construction thereof and actions taken thereunder shall be binding on all persons for the purposes so stated by the Administrator .
nodes.summary:
- Article 3 (Administration): Establishes the Administrator’s broad authority to interpret, construe, and run the Plan; correct defects, omissions, inconsistencies, and errors through equitable adjustments; and make final, binding decisions on Participants and Beneficiaries. The Administrator may delegate its powers, and such delegates are treated as the Administrator. References a Committee oversight limitation (Section 10.7).

- Article 4 (Eligibility/Participation): Limits participation to Employees meeting specific criteria to maintain “top-hat” status under ERISA. Enrollment is automatic for eligible Employees, though the Administrator may exclude certain Employees or groups. Unless otherwise determined, only Employees in Band 35+ are eligible. To participate, an Employee must (1) be a participant in a Company Qualified Retirement Plan, and (2) for the relevant Plan Year either have (or be deemed to have had) a prior-year Account, or have Total Pay (as defined under the RSP, without the Section 401(a)(17) limit) exceeding the Section 401(a)(17) compensation cap.

nodes.title: ELIGIBILITY
nodes.heading: ARTICLE 4 ELIGIBILITY
nodes.start_phrase: Participation in this Plan shall be limit ed to Employees who meet the requirements of Section 4.2, and shall automatically occur for such Employees, provided that the Administrator may designate, on a case-by-case basis, Employees or categories of Employees who shall not be eligible to participate in all or any portion of this Plan, and provided further , that the determination of eligible Empl oyees shall be made consistent with the requirement that the Plan be a “top-hat” plan for purposes of ERISA.
nodes.summary:
- Administration: The Plan is administered by an Administrator with broad authority (subject to certain Committee limits under Section 10.7) to interpret, construe, and operate the Plan. The Administrator can correct defects, supply omissions, reconcile inconsistencies, and make equitable adjustments for mathematical/accounting errors or similar mistakes. Decisions are final, conclusive, and binding on Participants and Beneficiaries. The Administrator may delegate its authority and responsibilities.
- Eligibility framework: Participation is limited to Employees meeting specified criteria and is automatic for those who qualify. The Administrator may designate specific Employees or categories as ineligible for all or part of the Plan. Eligibility determinations must align with the Plan’s status as an ERISA “top-hat” plan. Unless otherwise determined, Employees must be in Band 35 or above to be eligible.
- Participation requirements: To participate, an Employee must (a) be a participant in a Company-maintained Qualified Retirement Plan (per that plan’s eligibility rules), and (b) for the relevant Plan Year either (i) have an existing Account from a prior year (including being treated as having one if they previously declined participation that would have created an Account), or (ii) receive Total Pay (as defined under the RSP) in excess of the Section 401(a)(17) compensation limit, with Total Pay measured without regard to that limit.

nodes.title: Eligibility
nodes.heading: Section 4.1 Eligibility .
nodes.start_phrase: Participation in this Plan shall be limit ed to Employees who meet the requirements of Section 4.2, and shall automatically occur for such Employees, provided that the Administrator may designate, on a case-by-case basis, Employees or categories of Employees who shall not be eligible to participate in all or any portion of this Plan, and provided further , that the determination of eligible Empl oyees shall be made consistent with the requirement that the Plan be a “top-hat” plan for purposes of ERISA.
nodes.summary:
- Article 3 (Administration): The Plan is administered by an Administrator with broad authority to interpret, construe, and manage the Plan. The Administrator may correct defects, omissions, inconsistencies, and mathematical/accounting errors through equitable adjustments. Its decisions are final, conclusive, and binding on Participants and Beneficiaries. Authority may be delegated, and certain powers are subject to Committee limitations referenced in Section 10.7.

- Article 4 (Eligibility): Participation is limited to Employees who meet specific criteria and is automatic for those eligible, though the Administrator may exclude certain Employees or categories to maintain the Plan’s ERISA “top-hat” status. By default, Employees must be in Band 35 or above to be eligible.

- Participation requirements (Section 4.2): An Employee must (a) be a participant in a Company-maintained Qualified Retirement Plan (per that plan’s eligibility rules) and (b) for the relevant Plan Year either (i) have an existing Plan Account from a prior year (including being treated as having one if a prior participation offer was declined) or (ii) have Total Pay (as defined under the RSP without the Section 401(a)(17) limitation) that exceeds the Section 401(a)(17) compensation limit.

nodes.title: Participation
nodes.heading: Section 4.2 Participation .
nodes.start_phrase: To become a Participant in the Plan, an Employee must satisfy Section 4.1 and:
nodes.summary:
- Administration (Article 3)
  - The Plan is administered by an Administrator with broad authority to interpret, construe, and operate the Plan, subject to any limits the Committee may impose under the Plan.
  - The Administrator’s interpretations and actions are final, conclusive, and binding on all participants and beneficiaries.
  - The Administrator may correct defects, supply omissions, reconcile inconsistencies, and make equitable adjustments to correct mathematical, accounting, or similar errors.
  - Authority and responsibilities may be delegated, and references to the “Administrator” include duly delegated persons.

- Eligibility (Article 4)
  - Participation is limited to Employees meeting specified criteria and is generally automatic once eligible.
  - The Administrator may designate certain Employees or categories as ineligible, consistent with maintaining the Plan as an ERISA “top-hat” plan.
  - Unless otherwise determined, Employees must be in Band 35 or above to be eligible.
  - To participate, an Employee must:
    - Be a participant in a Company Qualified Retirement Plan; and
    - For the relevant Plan Year, satisfy at least one of:
      - Have (or be treated as having) a prior-year Account under this Plan;
      - Receive Total Pay above the Section 401(a)(17) compensation limit;
      - Be employed in Band 50 or above as of the prior-year Band 50 Determination Date (with Administrator discretion for newly hired/promoted Band 50 employees to join open enrollment); or
      - Accrue benefits under a Qualified Retirement Plan in excess of the Section 415 limit.

- Supplemental Benefits (Article 5, Section 5.1 – RP-related)
  - For Participants in the RP (excluding terminated participants), the Company establishes an RP-Related Account.
  - “Compensation” for RP credits follows the RP definition, with Committee discretion to modify; starting with the 2003 performance year, it includes the value of restricted stock granted in lieu of cash supplemental Annual Incentive Awards.
  - Contribution Credits to the RP-Related Account equal the excess of hypothetical RP credits calculated without the Section 401(a)(17) limit and ignoring deferrals, over the actual RP credits; no such credits are made for pay periods on or after July 1, 2007.
  - The benefits formula for a Plan Year is set by the Administrator and applied uniformly to similarly situated Participants.
  - Certain Participants, at the Company’s discretion and subject to special agreements (which control if conflicting), may be credited as if they had five additional Years of Service, with corresponding additional credits to their RP-Related Account.

nodes.title: SUPPLEMENTAL BENEFITS
nodes.heading: ARTICLE 5 SUPPLEMENT AL BENEFITS
nodes.start_phrase: If a Parti cipant is a participant under the RP, other than a terminated participa nt, the Company shall establish an RP-Related Account for such Participant, which shall be determined as follows:
nodes.summary:
- Eligibility highlights: Employees in Band 50 or above as of the Band 50 Determination Date in the prior Plan Year are eligible, with discretionary open-enrollment access for newly hired/promoted Band 50 employees after that date; eligibility also extends to individuals accruing benefits under a Qualified Retirement Plan in excess of the Section 415 limitation.
- Article 5 (Supplemental Benefits) establishes that Participants who are active participants in the RP (retirement plan), and not terminated, will have an RP-Related Account set up.
- Compensation for RP credits generally follows the RP’s definition, but the Committee may adjust what counts as Compensation; beginning with the 2003 performance year, the value of certain restricted stock awards granted in lieu of cash supplemental Annual Incentive Awards is included.
- Contribution Credits: Each Plan Year, an amount is credited equal to the excess of (x) hypothetical RP Contribution Credits calculated without the Section 401(a)(17) compensation cap and ignoring deferrals, over (y) the actual RP credits; no such credits apply for pay periods on or after July 1, 2007.
- Benefit formula: Determined by the Administrator and applied uniformly to similarly situated Participants.
- Additional service credit: The Company may, at its discretion, deem certain Participants to have five extra Years of Service, with corresponding additional credits to their RP-Related Account; any special agreement with a Participant controls if it conflicts with this section.

nodes.title: Benefits Under the RP
nodes.heading: Section 5.1 Benefits Under the RP.
nodes.start_phrase: If a Parti cipant is a participant under the RP, other than a terminated participa nt, the Company shall establish an RP-Related Account for such Participant, which shall be determined as follows:
nodes.summary:
- Eligibility highlights: participants include those in pay Band 50 or higher as of the Band 50 Determination Date (with Administrator discretion to include newly hired/promoted Band 50 employees for open enrollment) or those whose Qualified Retirement Plan benefits exceed the IRC Section 415 limit.
- Article 5 establishes supplemental benefits that provide make-up credits above qualified plan limits.

- Section 5.1 (RP supplemental benefits):
  - An RP-Related Account is created for eligible, non-terminated participants.
  - Compensation for RP credits follows the RP definition, with Committee discretion to modify; beginning with the 2003 performance year, includes certain restricted stock granted in lieu of cash supplemental Annual Incentive Awards.
  - Contribution Credits equal the excess of hypothetical RP credits calculated without the IRC Section 401(a)(17) compensation cap and including deferrals, over actual RP credits; no credits for pay periods on/after July 1, 2007.
  - Benefit formula is set by the Administrator and applied uniformly to similarly situated participants.
  - Additional Years of Service:
    - Company may, by special agreement, deem five additional Years of Service and credit the difference between cumulative credits with and without the added service; default five-year vesting with forfeiture upon termination before five years, except for death or disability.
    - Transition: participants with such agreements who lack five Years of Service as of July 1, 2007 receive 2007 credits as if the RP continued through December 31, 2007; no credits for 2008 or later.

- Section 5.2 (RSP supplemental benefits):
  - An RSP-Related Account is created for eligible, non-terminated participants.
  - Compensation for RSP credits equals “Total Pay” under the RSP, subject to Committee discretion; effective July 1, 2007, includes restricted stock granted in lieu of cash Annual Incentive Awards (subject to a cap).
  - Limitation for Band 50+ participants: Incentive Pay (including such restricted stock) counted only up to one times Base Salary; pay band/Base Salary determined as of January 1 (or upon hire/rehire); special rehire rule for contributions; limitation applies to amounts actually paid in the Plan Year, regardless of when earned.

nodes.title: Benefits in Excess of Limits Under the RSP
nodes.heading: Section 5.2 Benefits in Excess of Limits Under the RSP .
nodes.start_phrase: If a Participant is a participant in the RSP, other than a terminated participant, the Company shall establish an RSP-Related Account for such Participant, which shall be determined as follows:
nodes.summary:
- Establishes special RP-related credits for certain participants with individual agreements to make up benefits, calculated under Section 5.3, generally subject to five-year vesting and forfeiture upon termination other than death or disability. Participants with fewer than five Years of Service as of July 1, 2007 receive a 2007 Plan Year credit as if the RP remained in effect through December 31, 2007; no credits are provided for 2008 or later.
- Creates an RSP-Related Account for active RSP participants to provide benefits that exceed qualified plan limits:
  - Defines Compensation for RSP credits by reference to “Total Pay” under the RSP, with Committee discretion to modify; effective July 1, 2007 includes restricted stock granted in lieu of cash annual incentives, subject to limits.
  - Imposes a Band 50+ limitation excluding Incentive Pay (including in-lieu restricted stock) above one times Base Salary; pay band/Base Salary determined as of January 1 (or rehire date); Incentive Pay counted when paid. Temporary salary reductions from March 30, 2009 through January 3, 2010 are disregarded.
  - Contribution Credits:
    - Company Stock Contribution: 1% make-up on Compensation plus deferrals over qualified limits, reduced by actual RSP allocation; no credits for pay periods on/after July 1, 2007.
    - Company Profit-Sharing Contribution: make-up of discretionary/fixed-rate profit-sharing over Section 401(a)(17)/415 limits and deferrals; only vested portions are payable, non-vested forfeited.
    - Company Matching Contribution (effective January 1, 2017):
      - Match on nonqualified deferrals up to 6% of Compensation not counted under the RSP due to Section 401(a)(17) limits or deferrals (regardless of RSP contributions).
      - Additional match equal to what was excluded under the RSP solely due to Section 415 limits.
      - Vesting follows the RSP.
    - Company Conversion Contribution: make-up of conversion contributions over limits; none after December 31, 2017 for Band 50+ and after December 31, 2018 for below Band 50; suspended March 30, 2009–January 3, 2010 except for those retirement-eligible as of December 31, 2009; resumed thereafter at prior levels; only vested portions payable; Company reserves right to change.
    - Transition Contributions for certain Former GE Capital employees: make-up of RSP transition contributions until they expire (no contributions after March 31, 2011); if eligible for both conversion and transition, participant receives the greater; only vested portions payable.
    - No disability-related contributions are provided under this plan.
  - Additional Company Contribution for Additional Years of Service: for selected participants deemed to have five extra RSP Years of Service, an additional credit equal to 80% (or a lower agreed percentage) of base salary at hire, generally five-year vested with forfeiture on termination other than death/disability; calculated and credited per Section 5.3 and any special agreement.
- Section 5.3 governs crediting: timing and manner determined by the Administrator, generally mirroring qualified plans but not required; amounts related to RP Section 415 limitations may be estimated at Separation from Service using consistent, reasonable assumptions.

nodes.title: Crediting of Account
nodes.heading: Section 5.3 Cr editing of Account .
nodes.start_phrase: Amounts described in this Article 5 shall be credited to the Supplemental Account established for a Participant at such times and in such manner as may be determined by the Administrator .
nodes.summary:
- Transition/GE Capital transition contributions: At a Supplemental Distribution, only the vested portion (per the RSP) is payable; any non-vested portion is forfeited. The right to Transition Contributions expires when it does under the RSP; no Transition Contributions are made for periods after March 31, 2011.
- No disability contributions: Unlike the RSP, this Plan does not provide ongoing contributions due to disability.
- Company contributions for additional years of service (special agreements): The Company may, by special agreement, deem certain Participants to have five additional Years of Service under the RSP and credit an additional amount equal to up to 80% (or a lower agreed percentage) of base salary at hire (pre-deferral) for periods on/after January 1, 2008. Credits are calculated under Administrator procedures applied consistently, are generally subject to five-year vesting, and are forfeited upon termination before five years of actual service except in cases of death or RSP-defined disability. Amounts are credited to the Participant’s RSP-Related Account.
- Crediting of accounts (Section 5.3):
  - Timing/manner: Administrator determines; aims to align with Qualified Retirement Plans but is not required to do so.
  - Section 415 limitation make-up amounts for the RP are estimated at Separation from Service using consistent assumptions and credited immediately before Plan payments commence.
  - Special agreement (5.2(c)) credits are determined and credited on the one-year anniversary of the later of the special agreement date or employment start.
  - Company stock contributions (5.2(b)(i)) are credited to a Stock Fund subaccount consistent with Stock Fund practices.
  - Other contributions (profit-sharing, matching, conversion, GE Capital transition, and special agreement credits) are credited to RSP-Related Account subaccounts reflecting available RSP investment funds, subject to Stock Fund limits and redirection rules; no self-directed brokerage subaccount unless the Administrator permits.
  - The Administrator may establish additional book reserve accounts and set procedures for recognizing investment results.
- Supplemental benefits payment election (Section 5.4): Supplemental Benefits are paid in cash from the Company’s general assets in the form elected by the Participant. Existing Participants (including certain Prior SRP participants not in pay status as of December 31, 2004) may make elections under Administrator rules compliant with Section 409A.

nodes.title: Supplemental Benefits Payment Election
nodes.heading: Section 5.4 Suppl emental Benefits Payment Election .
nodes.start_phrase: Any Supplemental Benefits payable under the Plan shall be paid in cash from the general assets of the Company in the form elected by the Participant subject to the following:
nodes.summary:
- How and when supplemental retirement credits are posted:
  - Special agreement credits are generally determined and credited on the one‑year anniversary of the later of the special agreement date or employment start, with consistent procedures for similarly situated participants.
  - Company stock-related contributions are credited to an RSP‑Related Account in a Stock Fund subaccount, with amounts determined consistent with Stock Fund practices.
  - Other company contributions (profit-sharing, matching, conversion, GE Capital transition) and special agreement credits are credited to RSP‑Related Account subaccounts tied to available RSP investment funds, subject to limits on Stock Fund allocations and no self-directed brokerage subaccounts.
  - The Administrator may establish additional book reserve accounts and set procedures for reflecting gains, losses, interest, dividends, and other adjustments.

- Supplemental Benefits payment elections (Section 5.4) and Section 409A compliance:
  - Benefits are paid in cash from the company’s general assets, in a form elected by the participant.
  - Permissible forms: single lump sum or annual installments over 5, 10, or 15 years (for amounts not subject to the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election).
  - Transition rules for elections and modifications for participants around 2004–2005, including one-time changes by 12/31/2005 without the usual 5‑year additional deferral, as permitted by 409A transition guidance.
  - For participants first becoming eligible after 12/31/2005 (with detailed rules for those first eligible on/after 1/1/2012 or tied to Q4 2011 compensation):
    - Initial elections may not apply to certain early company contributions; those amounts default to an Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election.
    - Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election: default to a single lump-sum payable on the first January 1 or July 1 at least six months after the earliest of separation, disability, or death (or as soon as administratively feasible thereafter, but within 90 days). This automatic election cannot be modified.
    - Contributions outside the automatic periods are governed by the participant’s initial election.
    - Rehired participants are treated as newly eligible for post‑rehire contributions for election purposes.
  - Default rule if no valid, timely election: single lump sum on the first January 1 or July 1 at least six months after separation, disability, or death (or within 90 days thereafter).
  - One-time modification right (if not previously used) before separation: must comply with 409A (minimum five‑year additional deferral; effective 12 months after change). No changes allowed after separation. Rehired participants may use a new one‑time modification for post‑rehire elections.
  - Prior SRP Plan coordination, including exceptions for benefits already in pay status and non-reduction rules for certain pre‑2005 accelerations.

- Elective Deferrals eligibility and enrollment (Article 6):
  - Amex notifies eligible employees; erroneous notifications do not confer eligibility and related elections are void to the extent allowed by 409A.
  - Participation requires a timely Deferral Election; standard Deferral Benefits Eligibility Date is January 1.
  - Special 30‑day election window for employees first entering Band 50 (or first becoming eligible for a Qualified Retirement Plan while in Band 50); eligibility starts the first payroll period after the 30‑day window. The Administrator may coordinate special and open enrollment and limit special enrollment when appropriate.
  - For non‑Band 50 employees who become eligible by exceeding the 401(a)(17) compensation limit:
    - If eligibility occurs in the first three quarters, participation begins the following January 1 via open enrollment.
    - If eligibility occurs in the fourth quarter, participation begins the first pay period after the first day of the second month of the first calendar quarter of the following year.

nodes.title: ELECTIVE DEFERRALS
nodes.heading: ARTICLE 6 ELECTIVE DEFERRALS
nodes.start_phrase: Employees eligible to participate in the Plan for a Plan Year with respect to Deferral Benefits will be notified by Amex of their eligibility to participate for such Plan Year.
nodes.summary:
- Article 6 governs Elective Deferrals, outlining how employees are notified of eligibility, how they become participants, and key timing rules.
- Section 6.1 (Notification): Amex notifies eligible employees each Plan Year. An erroneous notice does not create eligibility; any deferral election by an ineligible person is void to the extent allowed under Section 409A. Eligibility/exclusions reference Sections 4.2 and 4.1.
- Section 6.2 (Participation): To participate for a Plan Year, eligible employees must make a Deferral Election per Section 6.5. Employees who were participants as of the prior year’s Band 50 Determination Date, or who are in Band 50+ by that date (or become Band 50+ before the end of the prior year and are authorized to enroll), can participate. The standard Deferral Benefits Eligibility Date is January 1 of the Plan Year.
- Special rules (per Section 6.3):
  - New to Band 50+: Employees first employed in Band 50+ (or already Band 50+ who newly become eligible for a Qualified Retirement Plan) are eligible as of that event and have 30 days to file an election; their Deferral Benefits Eligibility Date is the first payroll period after that 30-day window. The Administrator may coordinate or limit special enrollment near year-end.
  - Not in Band 50+:
    - If an employee first qualifies during the first three quarters by exceeding the Section 401(a)(17) compensation limit, eligibility to participate begins January 1 of the following Plan Year (with access to open enrollment).
    - If first qualifying in the final calendar quarter by exceeding the Section 401(a)(17) limit, eligibility begins the first pay period starting after the first day of the second month of the first quarter of the following year (sentence continues beyond the excerpt).

nodes.title: Notification
nodes.heading: Section 6.1 Notifi cation .
nodes.start_phrase: Employees eligible to participate in the Plan for a Plan Year with respect to Deferral Benefits will be notified by Amex of their eligibility to participate for such Plan Year.
nodes.summary:
- Article 6 covers Elective Deferrals: how eligibility is communicated, who can participate each Plan Year, when elections can be made, and when eligibility starts.
- Section 6.1 (Notification): Amex notifies employees of eligibility. An erroneous notice does not create eligibility; any deferral election by an ineligible person is void to the extent permitted under Section 409A.
- Section 6.2 (Participation): 
  - An employee becomes a Participant for Deferral Benefits in a Plan Year by making a Deferral Election under Section 6.5 if they:
    - Were a Participant in the prior Plan Year as of the Band 50 Determination Date, or
    - Are employed in Band 50 or above as of that prior-year Band 50 Determination Date, or
    - Become Band 50 or above (or first become eligible while Band 50 or above) before the end of the prior Plan Year and are authorized to enroll.
  - Standard Deferral Benefits Eligibility Date is January 1 of the Plan Year.
  - Special rules (per Section 6.3):
    - (a) New to Plan and in Band 50+ (or become eligible for a Qualified Retirement Plan while remaining Band 50+): may file an election within 30 days of becoming eligible; Deferral Benefits Eligibility Date is the first payroll period after that 30-day window. The Administrator may coordinate special and open enrollments and limit special enrollment when appropriate.
    - (b) Not in Band 50+; eligibility triggered by exceeding the IRC Section 401(a)(17) compensation limit:
      - If the limit is first exceeded in the first three quarters: eligible January 1 of the following Plan Year and may enroll during open enrollment.
      - If first exceeded in the final calendar quarter: eligible as of the first pay period beginning after the first day of the second month of the first calendar quarter of the following year.

nodes.title: Participation
nodes.heading: Section 6.2 Participation .
nodes.start_phrase: An eligible Employee for a Plan Year who was a Participant in the prior Plan Year as of the Band 50 Determinat ion Date, or who is employed in Band 50 or above as of the Band 50 Determination Date in the prior Plan Year, or who otherwise becomes employed in Band 50 or above or first becomes eligible while in Band 50 or above prior to the end of the prior Plan Year and is authorized by the Administrator to participate in enrollme nt shall become a Participant in the Plan with respect to Deferra l Benefits for such Plan Year by making a Deferral Election in accordance with Section 6.5 for the Plan Year.
nodes.summary:
- Article 6 governs Elective Deferrals, detailing eligibility notifications, participation rules, special enrollment timing, and 409A compliance.
- Section 6.1 (Notification): Amex notifies eligible employees each Plan Year; erroneous notices do not confer eligibility. Any deferral election by an ineligible individual is void to the extent allowed under Section 409A.
- Section 6.2 (Participation):
  - Who can participate: Employees who were prior-year Participants as of the Band 50 Determination Date, are Band 50+ as of that date, or who become Band 50+ (or otherwise first become eligible while Band 50+) before the end of the prior Plan Year and are authorized to enroll. Participation is by making a Deferral Election (per Section 6.5). Deferral Benefits Eligibility Date is January 1 of the Plan Year.
  - Special rules:
    - (a) New Band 50+ entrants (or those in Band 50+ who newly become eligible for a Qualified Retirement Plan) may file an election within 30 days; eligibility begins the first payroll period after that 30-day window. The Administrator may coordinate or limit special enrollment near year-end.
    - (b) Employees not in Band 50+ who first become eligible by exceeding the Section 401(a)(17) compensation limit:
      - If this occurs in the first three quarters, eligibility begins January 1 of the following Plan Year (open enrollment applies).
      - If it occurs in the final quarter, eligibility begins the first pay period after the first day of the second month of the first calendar quarter of the following Plan Year; advance elections allowed by the Administrator’s deadline in accordance with Section 6.3.
      - Clarifications: Exceeding the Section 415 limit alone does not create special enrollment; the date of exceeding 401(a)(17) is based on Plan Year Compensation even if some pay is excluded from Supplemental Benefits due to unfulfilled service requirements.
    - (c) Mid-year elections are generally prohibited unless expressly permitted and compliant with Section 6.3; must meet Administrator deadlines. All Deferral Elections become irrevocable by the day before the Deferral Benefits Eligibility Date (or earlier if set by the Administrator).
- Section 6.3 (Newly Eligible Employees): Consistent with Section 409A and Section 6.2, mid-year enrollment may be offered to employees who newly become eligible and were not previously eligible for an Amex elective account-balance deferred compensation arrangement. Employees previously eligible may still be treated as newly eligible (and allowed mid-year enrollment) if either:
  - (a) They received full payout of all prior elective account-balance amounts and were not eligible to continue participation at the time of the last payment (ignoring any right to delay payment); or
  - (b) They had ceased eligibility under all such plans and were not eligible at any time during the preceding 24 months before re-eligibility (ignoring mere rights to accrue earnings), regardless of whether prior deferrals have been paid.
- Section 6.4 (Deferrable Compensation): Introduces “Eligible Compensation,” but the substantive content is not included in the excerpt.

nodes.title: Newly Eligible Employees
nodes.heading: Section 6.3 Newl y Eligible Employees .
nodes.start_phrase: To the extent perm issible under Section 409A and Section 6.2, Employees who become eligible to participate in the Plan during a Plan Year with respect to Deferral Benefits and who have not previously been eligible to participate in an elective account-balance deferred compensation arrangement (as defined for purposes of Section 409A) of Amex or its subsidiaries may be offered by Amex the opportunity to participate in the Plan for the Plan Year in accordance with Section 6.2.
nodes.summary:
- Sets rules for timing and irrevocability of deferral elections: employees may elect before the Deferral Benefits Eligibility Date (first day of the relevant pay period) by the Administrator’s deadline; elections become irrevocable no later than the day before that date (or an earlier Administrator-set date).
- Clarifies no special mid-year enrollment right arises merely because an employee exceeds the Internal Revenue Code Section 415 limit under a qualified plan.
- Clarifies that the date an employee exceeds the Section 401(a)(17) compensation limit is based on total Plan Year compensation, even if some compensation is excluded from supplemental benefits due to unmet service requirements for company contributions.
- Generally prohibits mid-year elections; any permitted mid-year election must also satisfy Section 6.3 and be filed by the Administrator’s deadline.
- Defines “Newly Eligible Employees” under Section 6.3 consistent with Section 409A and Section 6.2:
  - Employees newly eligible during a Plan Year who were not previously eligible for an Amex elective account-balance deferred compensation arrangement may be offered participation for that year.
  - Employees previously eligible may be treated as newly eligible (and allowed mid-year enrollment) if either:
    - They received all payments from this and any other elective account-balance plan and, at the last payment date, were not eligible to continue participation (ignoring any payment delay rights), or
    - They ceased eligibility and were not eligible to participate in any such plan at any time during the prior 24 months before re-eligibility (ignoring earnings accrual rights), regardless of whether prior deferrals have been paid.
- Introduces Section 6.4 on Deferrable Compensation, beginning with “Eligible Compensation” (details not included in the excerpt).

nodes.title: Deferrable Compensation
nodes.heading: Section 6.4 Deferrable Compensation .
nodes.start_phrase: An eligible Employee for a Plan Year may elect to defer a specified amount from one or more of the following items:
nodes.summary:
- Clarifies mid-year deferral elections: generally prohibited except as expressly permitted under Sections 6.2 and 6.3; any permitted mid-year election must meet Section 6.3 requirements, be filed by the Administrator’s deadline, and becomes irrevocable as of the day before the Deferral Benefits Eligibility Date (or earlier if set by the Administrator).
- Provides clarifications on statutory limits: no special enrollment right arises from exceeding the Section 415 limit; the date an Employee exceeds the Section 401(a)(17) compensation limit is determined on Plan Year Compensation, even if some compensation is excluded from supplemental benefit calculations due to service requirements.
- Defines when “newly eligible” mid-year participation is allowed under Section 409A: 
  - Employees not previously eligible for an Amex elective account-balance deferred compensation plan may be offered participation mid-year.
  - Previously eligible Employees may be treated as newly eligible if (a) they received full payout of all elective account-balance plans and were not eligible to continue at the last payment date, or (b) they had ceased eligibility and were not eligible under any such plan for at least 24 months before re-eligibility (ignoring rights to delay payment or to accrue earnings).
- Specifies deferrable compensation:
  - Standard elections may include Base Salary for the Plan Year and Incentive Pay payable in the second Plan Year after the election (excluding amounts earned before the start of the Plan Year following the filing).
  - Mid-year/newly eligible elections may include Base Salary for payroll periods beginning on/after the Deferral Benefits Eligibility Date and a prorated portion of Incentive Pay payable in the following Plan Year based on days remaining in the year or performance period.
- Sets maximum deferral limits and methodology:
  - Administrator imposes limits and may waive them before the election becomes effective.
  - Aggregate deferrals from Base Salary (next Plan Year) and Incentive Pay (second following Plan Year) are capped by reference to 100% of a specified Base Salary rate as of set dates, with special rules for mid-year eligibility due to Band 50 status or exceeding the 401(a)(17) limit.
  - Provides a formula to cap Incentive Pay deferral based on the remaining percentage after the Base Salary deferral election.
  - Deferrals cannot exceed net cash amounts after withholdings.
  - Administrator may set stricter caps (current default maximum of 85% of Incentive Pay).
- Outlines computation methods: Administrator may require elections as percentages, dollar amounts, or other reasonable methods; may allow multiple methods; may let elections apply only to compensation above the Section 401(a)(17) limit.
- Details deferral election procedures:
  - Timing: generally due by December 15 of the preceding Plan Year (or the next Monday if Dec 15 falls on a weekend), with separate deadlines for permitted mid-year elections.
  - Form: as prescribed by the Administrator.
  - Contents: must specify the compensation items and amounts within plan limits; includes additional provisions for Band 50 employees (text continues beyond the excerpt).

nodes.title: Deferral Benefits Election
nodes.heading: Section 6.5 Deferral Benefits Election .
nodes.start_phrase: An eligible Emplo yee for a Plan Year who wants to participate in the Plan with respect to Deferral Benefits for a Plan Year must make an irrevocable Deferral Election for the Plan Year on or before the December 15 of the preceding Plan Year, or if December 15 is on a weekend, the following Monday , or as of such other deadline as the Administrator may establish (but in all events prior to the beginning of such Plan Year);
nodes.summary:
- Sets limits on Deferral Elections:
  - Deferrals cannot exceed amounts otherwise payable in cash, net of applicable withholdings.
  - The Administrator may impose additional limits on deferral amounts/percentages before elections take effect; by default, up to 85% of Incentive Pay may be deferred.
  - Clarifies that actual Base Salary paid may change the dollar amount deferred but does not change the maximum Incentive Pay limit tied to prior periods.

- Defines how deferral amounts can be computed:
  - Elections may be stated as percentages or dollar amounts of Base Salary and/or Incentive Pay, or via another reasonable method selected by the Administrator.
  - The Administrator may allow multiple calculation methods or require one.
  - Elections may apply only to compensation above the Section 401(a)(17) Limitation.

- Establishes timing and process for Deferral Benefits Elections (Section 6.5):
  - Elections are irrevocable and generally must be made by December 15 of the preceding Plan Year (or the next Monday if that date falls on a weekend), and in all cases before the Plan Year begins.
  - Mid‑year eligibility allows a later deadline per Section 6.2, or an earlier Administrator‑set deadline.
  - Elections must be made in the form and by the deadlines the Administrator prescribes.

- Specifies required election content:
  - The compensation items to defer (eligible under Section 6.4(a)) and the amount of each, subject to Section 6.4(b) and any administrative limits.

- Provides special time and form of payment elections for Band 50 and above:
  - Eligible Band 50 Employees may elect payment timing: either upon Separation from Service or on a specified date at least five years after the last day of the Plan Year.
  - They may elect payment form: lump sum or substantially equal annual installments over 5, 10, or 15 years.
  - Default if no valid time and form are elected: lump‑sum payment on the January 1 or July 1 that is at least six months after Separation from Service (or as soon as administratively feasible thereafter, but no later than 90 days).
  - Employees below Band 50 cannot make special time/form elections; their Deferral Benefits follow the Supplemental Election under Section 5.4. Newly hired/promoted/transferred Band 50 employees may be allowed to participate in open enrollment for the following Plan Year.

- Details withholding mechanics:
  - Base Salary deferrals are withheld from each regular payroll.
  - Incentive Pay deferrals are withheld when the Incentive Pay is (or would be) paid.

- Addresses crediting and accounts:
  - The Administrator maintains a Deferral Account for each Participant’s Deferral Benefits and may use subaccounts to track earnings/losses per Article 7.
  - Article 7 earnings: each Participant’s RP‑Related Account (per Section 5.1) is credited not less than annually with Imputed Earnings Credits, at the same interest rate and in a similar manner as under the RP.

nodes.title: Crediting of Deferred Amounts
nodes.heading: Section 6.6 Crediting of Deferr ed Amounts .
nodes.start_phrase: The Administrator shall establish and maintain a Deferral Account with respect to each Participant’ s Deferral Benefits.
nodes.summary:
- Participants must elect both the time and form of payment for each Plan Year’s Deferral Benefits:
  - Time: either upon Separation from Service or a specified date at least five years after the end of the Plan Year.
  - Form: lump sum or substantially equal annual installments over 5, 10, or 15 years.
- Default rule if a valid time and form are not both elected: payment will be a lump sum on the first January 1 or July 1 at least six months after Separation from Service (or as soon as administratively feasible thereafter, but no later than 90 days).
- Eligibility clarification on special elections:
  - Employees below Band 50 as of the prior Plan Year’s Band 50 Determination Date cannot make a special time/form election; the Supplemental Election under Section 5.4 applies.
  - New Participants who become Band 50 (by hire, promotion, or transfer) after that date may be allowed to participate in the next open enrollment as Band 50 or above.
- Withholding of deferrals:
  - Base Salary deferrals are withheld from each regular payroll.
  - Incentive Pay deferrals are withheld when the incentive is or would be paid.
- Crediting of deferrals:
  - The Administrator establishes a Deferral Account for each Participant and credits deferred amounts at times and in manners it determines.
  - Accounts may be divided into subaccounts to track earnings and losses per Article 7.
- Earnings (Article 7):
  - Each Participant’s RP-Related Account is credited, at least annually, with Imputed Earnings Credits (as defined in the RP), using the same interest rate and similar computation method as under the RP, under procedures and timing set by the Administrator and applied consistently to similarly situated Participants.

nodes.title: EARNINGS
nodes.heading: ARTICLE 7 EARNINGS
nodes.start_phrase: For each Participan t, the RP-Related Account established pursuant to Section 5.1 shall be increased by the Imputed Earnings Credit (as such term is defined in the RP), not less frequently than annually , under procedures and at times determ ined by the Administrator and consistently applied for similarly situated Participants.
nodes.summary:
- Participants must elect both the payment timing and form for each Plan Year’s deferral: timing is either upon Separation from Service or a specified date at least five years after the Plan Year; form is a lump sum or 5, 10, or 15 annual installments.
- If an election does not validly specify both timing and form, the default is a lump-sum payment on January 1 or July 1 at least six months after Separation from Service (or as soon as administratively feasible thereafter, but within 90 days).
- Only employees at Band 50 or above as of the prior Plan Year’s Band 50 Determination Date may make special time-and-form elections for that Plan Year; others are governed by the Supplemental Election under Section 5.4.
- New participants who become Band 50 or above after the Determination Date may be permitted to join open enrollment for the following Plan Year as Band 50+.
- Deferral withholding: Base Salary deferrals are taken from each regular paycheck; Incentive Pay deferrals are withheld when the incentive is (or would be) paid.
- The Administrator establishes a Deferral Account for each participant, credits deferred amounts at times/manners it determines, and may use subaccounts to track earnings and losses per Article 7.
- Earnings (Article 7): Each participant’s RP-Related Account is credited, at least annually, with Imputed Earnings Credits (as defined in the RP), using the same interest rate and similar computation methods as the RP, applied consistently to similarly situated participants.

nodes.title: RP-Related Account
nodes.heading: Section 7.1 RP-R elated Account .
nodes.start_phrase: For each Participan t, the RP-Related Account established pursuant to Section 5.1 shall be increased by the Imputed Earnings Credit (as such term is defined in the RP), not less frequently than annually , under procedures and at times determ ined by the Administrator and consistently applied for similarly situated Participants.
nodes.summary:
- Participants must elect both the time and form of payment for each Plan Year’s Deferral Benefits:
  - Time: either upon Separation from Service or a specified date at least five years after the end of the Plan Year.
  - Form: either a lump sum or substantially equal annual installments over 5, 10, or 15 years.
- Default rule if an election is incomplete or invalid: payment will be a lump sum on the first January 1 or July 1 that is at least six months after Separation from Service (or as soon as administratively feasible thereafter, but no later than 90 days).
- Eligibility limits for special elections:
  - Employees not in Band 50 or above as of the prior Plan Year’s Band 50 Determination Date cannot file a special time/form election; their Supplemental Election under Section 5.4 applies.
  - New Participants who become Band 50 or above after that date may be allowed by the Administrator to join open enrollment for the following Plan Year as Band 50 or above.
- Withholding of deferrals:
  - Base Salary deferrals are withheld from each regular payroll.
  - Incentive Pay deferrals are withheld when the Incentive Pay is (or would be) paid.
- Crediting of deferred amounts:
  - The Administrator maintains a Deferral Account for each Participant and credits deferrals at times/manner it determines; subaccounts may be used to track earnings/losses under Article 7.
- Earnings (Article 7, Section 7.1):
  - Each Participant’s RP-Related Account receives Imputed Earnings Credits (as defined in the RP) at least annually, under consistent procedures, at the same interest rate and computed similarly to the RP for each Plan Year.

nodes.title: RSP-Related Account
nodes.heading: Section 7.2 RSP -Related Account .
nodes.start_phrase: A Partic ipant’ s RSP-Related Account shall be credited with earnings under the Hypothetical Investment Method set forth below .
nodes.summary:
- Section 7.2 establishes that a Participant’s RSP-Related Account is credited with earnings using the Hypothetical Investment Method.
- Section 7.3 (Deferral Accounts) sets how Deferral Benefits earn returns by role and time period:
  - (a) For Plan Year 2011 and later, Deferral Benefits earn under the Hypothetical Investment Method; 2010 Incentive Pay paid in 2011 is treated as 2010 Deferral Benefits.
  - (b) Executive Officers: For pre-2011 Plan Years, earnings credited in Plan Years beginning on/after January 1, 2011 use the Hypothetical Investment Method; earnings credited in 2010 and prior use the Interest Method. 2010 earnings (not paid by October 27, 2010) are capped at the AFR if Amex’s ROE is below the target range; amounts paid before October 27, 2010 used the Interest Method without the AFR cap.
  - (c) Non-Executive Officers: For pre-2011 Plan Years, earnings use the Interest Method through December 31, 2011. If a Participant becomes an Executive Officer during 2011, 2011 earnings on pre-2011 benefits are capped at the AFR (except amounts already paid above AFR). From 2012 onward, the Hypothetical Investment Method applies.
  - (d) Retirees: For pre-2011 Plan Years, earnings use the Interest Method through December 31, 2012; the Hypothetical Investment Method applies effective January 1, 2013.
- Section 7.4 (Hypothetical Investment Method) allows Participants to direct credits among subaccounts described in Section 5.3. For Deferral Benefits from pre-2011 Plan Years, Participants may elect an option crediting earnings at the AFR instead of the Stock Fund or RSP-based options.
- Company Stock limits: transfers to the Stock Fund are prohibited if they would cause Company Stock to exceed 10% of the value of the relevant Deferral Account or RSP-Related Account at the time of transfer; there is also a cap of no more than 10% of new contributions directed to the Stock Fund (sentence truncated in the excerpt).
- Key defined terms referenced include Hypothetical Investment Method, Interest Method, AFR (Applicable Federal Rate), ROE target range, RSP-based investment options, and Stock Fund.

nodes.title: Deferral Accounts
nodes.heading: Section 7.3 Deferral Accounts .
nodes.start_phrase: For Plan Year 2011 and later, a Participant’ s Deferral Benefits for such Plan Year shall be credited with earnings under the Hypothet ical Investment Method set forth below .
nodes.summary:
- Section 7.2 establishes that a Participant’s RSP-Related Account is credited with earnings under the Hypothetical Investment Method.
- Section 7.3 outlines how Deferral Accounts are credited with earnings, varying by plan year and participant status:
  - From Plan Year 2011 onward, Deferral Benefits are credited under the Hypothetical Investment Method; 2010 Incentive Pay paid in 2011 is treated as 2010 Deferral Benefits.
  - Executive Officers: For Deferral Benefits from pre-2011 plan years, earnings credited in plan years beginning on/after Jan 1, 2011 use the Hypothetical Investment Method; earnings credited in 2010 and earlier use the Interest Method. 2010 earnings (if not paid by Oct 27, 2010) are capped at the AFR if Amex’s ROE is below the target range; amounts paid before Oct 27, 2010 used the Interest Method without the AFR cap.
  - Non-Executive Officers: For pre-2011 Deferral Benefits, earnings are under the Interest Method through Dec 31, 2011; if the participant becomes an Executive Officer during 2011, 2011 earnings on those pre-2011 deferrals are capped at the AFR (except amounts already paid above AFR before the status change). From 2012 onward, the Hypothetical Investment Method applies.
  - Retirees: For pre-2011 Deferral Benefits, earnings are under the Interest Method through Dec 31, 2012, shifting to the Hypothetical Investment Method effective Jan 1, 2013.
- Section 7.4 describes the Hypothetical Investment Method:
  - Participants may direct credits among subaccounts described in Section 5.3 for both RSP-Related and Deferral Accounts (to the extent subject to this method).
  - For Deferral Benefits from pre-2011 plan years, participants may elect an investment option crediting earnings at the AFR instead of the Stock Fund or RSP-based options.
  - Company stock concentration limits: transfers to the Stock Fund are prohibited if they would cause Company Stock to exceed 10% of the total value of the participant’s Deferral Account (for Deferral Account investments) or 10% of the RSP-Related Account (for RSP-Related investments).
  - The text indicates an additional restriction on directing more than 10% of new contributions to the Stock Fund (sentence truncated).

nodes.title: Hypothetical Investment Method
nodes.heading: Section 7.4 Hypothetical Investment Method .
nodes.start_phrase: For each Participant, credits to his or her RSP-Related and Deferral Account (to the extent subject to the Hypothetical Investment Method) shall be made to such subaccounts thereunder as directed by such Participant, using the subaccounts described in Section 5.3,
nodes.summary:
