- Establishes how earnings are credited to Participants’ RSP-Related and Deferral Accounts, primarily via the Hypothetical Investment Method, with specific transition rules from the Interest Method based on participant status and plan years.
- Section 7.2: RSP-Related Accounts always earn under the Hypothetical Investment Method.
- Section 7.3 (Deferral Accounts):
  - 2011 and later Plan Years: Deferral Benefits earn under the Hypothetical Investment Method. 2010 Incentive Pay paid in 2011 and deferred is treated as 2010 Deferral Benefits.
  - Executive Officers: For pre-2011 Plan Years, earnings credited in Plan Years beginning on/after Jan 1, 2011 use the Hypothetical Investment Method; earnings credited in 2010 and prior Plan Years use the Interest Method. 2010 earnings (not paid by Oct 27, 2010) are capped at AFR if Amex’s ROE is below target; amounts paid before Oct 27, 2010 used the Interest Method without the AFR cap.
  - Non-Executive Officers: For pre-2011 Plan Years, earnings use the Interest Method through Dec 31, 2011; if the participant becomes an Executive Officer during 2011, 2011 earnings on pre-2011 Deferral Benefits are capped at AFR (except amounts already paid above AFR before becoming an Executive Officer). From 2012 forward, the Hypothetical Investment Method applies.
  - Retirees: For pre-2011 Plan Years, earnings use the Interest Method through Dec 31, 2012; the Hypothetical Investment Method applies beginning Jan 1, 2013.
- Section 7.4 (Hypothetical Investment Method mechanics):
  - Participants allocate credits among subaccounts (per RSP investment options), in 1% increments, with change frequency generally mirroring RSP rules and any additional plan rules.
  - For pre-2011 Deferral Benefits, a Participant may elect an AFR-based option instead of the Stock Fund or RSP-based options.
  - Stock Fund concentration limits: no transfers or new contributions that would cause Company Stock holdings in either the Deferral Account or RSP-Related Account to exceed 10% of that Account’s total value; no more than 10% of new contributions to either Account may be directed to the Stock Fund. Any excess is redirected to the Plan’s default fund.
  - Subaccounts track the actual performance (dividends, gains/losses) of the elected funds (or AFR, if chosen). Transfers among funds follow RSP-like rules, subject to Plan-specific limits and Administrator rules. Failure to elect results in investment in an Administrator-selected default fund (generally the RSP default), and the Administrator may exclude certain RSP funds (including any self-directed brokerage) from availability.
  - Valuation follows uniform Administrator rules aiming to mirror timing and market factors used in the RSP.
- Section 7.5 (Interest Method for applicable Deferral Accounts):
  - Annual crediting at the applicable Schedule Rate, subject to plan limits.
  - Vesting: principal is always 100% vested. Until Jan 1, 2011, earnings at the Minimum Schedule Rate vest as credited; earnings above the Minimum Schedule Rate vest upon Retirement Eligibility, or earlier death/Disability. Effective Dec 31, 2010, all unpaid Interest Method earnings became fully vested.
- Section 7.6 (Special Restrictions for Insiders):
  - Applies to Insiders while they are Insiders and during any post-cessation period requiring reporting under Exchange Act Rule 16a-2(b); ceases when Insider status (and any such period) ends. Begins automatically when a Participant becomes an Insider.
  - Imposes additional limits on Insider investment credits and transfers (text partially truncated), intended to restrict certain subaccount allocations, especially those tied to Company Stock.

nodes.title: Interest Method
nodes.heading: Section 7.5 Inter est Method .
nodes.start_phrase: (a) Under the Interest Method, a Participant’ s Deferral Account for a Plan Year shall be credited with interest equivalents each calendar year at the Schedule Rate in effect for the calendar year, subject to any limitations established under the Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Default investment designation: If a participant does not make an investment election, the Administrator will direct amounts to a default subaccount (generally the RSP’s default fund unless otherwise directed). The Administrator may exclude one or more RSP investment options, including any self-directed brokerage account, from being available under this Plan.
- Subaccount valuation: The Administrator will value subaccounts under uniform, reasonable rules intended to mirror the timing, manner, and market fluctuation factors used for comparable investments in the RSP, subject to administrative practicality.
- Interest Method (Section 7.5):
  - Crediting: Deferral Accounts using the Interest Method are credited annually with interest equivalents at the applicable Schedule Rate, subject to Plan limits.
  - Vesting:
    - Principal: Always 100% vested.
    - Earnings before 1/1/2011: Earnings at the Minimum Schedule Rate vest as credited; earnings above the Minimum Schedule Rate vest upon Retirement Eligibility or earlier death or Disability, and thereafter as credited.
    - Effective 12/31/2010: All unpaid earnings under the Interest Method become fully vested.
- Special Restrictions for Insiders (Section 7.6):
  - Applicability: Applies during any period a participant is an Insider, including post-cessation reporting periods under Exchange Act Rule 16a-2(b); automatically applies upon becoming an Insider and ceases after Insider status and any required reporting period end.
  - Funding restrictions: Credits to an Insider’s Account may not be directed to certain subaccounts (text truncated, but indicates limitations on where Insiders’ credits can be invested).

nodes.title: Special Restrictions
nodes.heading: Section 7.6 Special Restrictions .
nodes.start_phrase: (a) The provisions of this Section 7.6 shall apply to Insiders.
nodes.summary:
- Investment fund designations and valuation:
  - If a participant does not choose an investment option, amounts default to the Administrator-selected subaccount, typically the RSP’s default fund.
  - The Administrator may exclude certain RSP funds (including any self-directed brokerage account) from being available under the Plan.
  - Subaccounts are valued under uniform rules intended to mirror timing, manner, and market fluctuation factors used for comparable RSP investments, subject to administrative practicality.

- Interest Method for Deferral Accounts (Section 7.5):
  - Accounts earn interest equivalents each calendar year at the applicable Schedule Rate, subject to Plan limits.
  - Vesting:
    - Principal is always 100% vested.
    - Earnings before January 1, 2011: amounts up to the Minimum Schedule Rate vest as credited; earnings above that rate vest upon Retirement Eligibility or earlier death/disability.
    - Effective December 31, 2010: all Interest Method earnings on unpaid Deferral Benefits become fully vested.

- Special restrictions for Insiders (Section 7.6):
  - Apply while an individual is an Insider and during any required post-cessation reporting period under Rule 16a-2(b).
  - Restrictions:
    - No credits to a Stock Fund subaccount for Insiders.
    - No transfers into a Stock Fund subaccount at any time.
    - Credits (including any made pre-Insider status to a Stock Fund subaccount) cannot be transferred, withdrawn, paid, or otherwise changed except:
      - As per the participant’s payment election or death distribution rules, but only when permitted by securities laws (with any delay limited to what those laws require and consistent with Section 409A).
      - Under applicable Plan forfeiture provisions.
  - The Plan intends these provisions to qualify for the Rule 16b-3(d) exemption from Exchange Act Section 16; the Administrator will administer accordingly.

- Payment of Supplemental Benefits (Article 8, Section 8.1; excluding death/disability):
  - Rules apply separately to amounts under the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election and other Supplemental Elections, if they differ.
  - Timing:
    - Lump sum: paid on the first January 1 or July 1 at least six months after Separation from Service (other than death/disability), within an administrative window not exceeding 90 days.
    - Installments: begin July 1 of the calendar year following Separation from Service (other than death/disability), within 90 days, and continue each July 1 (within 90 days) for the elected period.
  - Re-employment does not alter ongoing payment schedules established at Separation from Service.
  - If a one-time modification to the initial Supplemental Election (per Section 5.4(a)(ii) or 5.4(d)) is effective before Separation from Service, payments follow the modified election.

nodes.title: PAYMENT OF BENEFITS
nodes.heading: ARTICLE 8 PAYMENT OF BENEFITS
nodes.start_phrase: By way of clarification, the rules set forth in this Section shall be applied separately to the portion of the Participant’ s Supple mental Benefits that is subject to the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election and the remainder of the Participant’ s Supplemental Benefits that is not covered by the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election, to the extent that the Participant’ s Supplemental Electi on differs from the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election.
nodes.summary:
- Insider restrictions related to the Stock Fund:
  - Insiders cannot transfer credits to a subaccount that tracks Stock Fund performance.
  - Any credits in an Insider’s account (including Stock Fund subaccounts funded before Insider status) cannot be transferred, withdrawn, paid out, or changed except:
    - Under the participant’s payment election or death distribution rules, and only when permitted by securities rules (with delays only as required, consistent with Section 409A), or
    - Under the Plan’s forfeiture provisions.
  - The Plan intends Stock Fund performance crediting for Insiders to be exempt from Section 16 under Exchange Act Rule 16b-3(d); the Administrator will interpret and administer the Plan to maintain this exemption.

- Article 8 – Payment of Benefits; Section 8.1 (Supplemental Account Payments other than for death or disability):
  - Clarifies that payment rules apply separately to:
    - The portion subject to the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election, and
    - Any remaining portion governed by the participant’s own Supplemental Election, to the extent they differ.
  - Payment timing following Separation from Service (other than due to death or Disability):
    - Lump sum: payable on the first January 1 or July 1 at least six months after separation, as soon as administratively feasible but no later than 90 days thereafter.
    - Annual installments: commence July 1 of the calendar year following separation, with each subsequent July 1 payment as soon as administratively feasible but within 90 days.
  - Payments continue on the elected schedule even if the participant is re-employed after separation.
  - If a participant made a one-time modification to the initial Supplemental Election under Sections 5.4(a)(ii) or 5.4(d), and it became effective before separation, the modified election governs the timing of Supplemental Benefits to the extent applicable.

nodes.title: Supplemental Account Payments (Other than Payments Due to Death or Disability)
nodes.heading: Section 8.1 Supplemental Account Payments (Other than Payments Due to Death or Disability) .
nodes.start_phrase: By way of clarification, the rules set forth in this Section shall be applied separately to the portion of the Participant’ s Supple mental Benefits that is subject to the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election and the remainder of the Participant’ s Supplemental Benefits that is not covered by the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election, to the extent that the Participant’ s Supplemental Electi on differs from the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election.
nodes.summary:
- Insider restrictions related to the Stock Fund:
  - Amounts credited to an Insider’s account cannot be transferred into a Stock Fund subaccount while the individual is an Insider.
  - Amounts in a Stock Fund subaccount that were credited when the individual was not an Insider, and any amounts in an Insider’s account, cannot be transferred, withdrawn, paid, or otherwise changed except:
    - As provided by the participant’s payment election,
    - Under death distribution rules but only when permitted by securities laws (with delays only as required and consistent with Section 409A), or
    - Under applicable forfeiture provisions.
  - The plan intends Stock Fund performance credits for Insiders to qualify for the Exchange Act Section 16 exemption under Rule 16b-3(d); the Administrator will interpret/administer the plan to preserve this exemption.

- Article 8: Payment of Benefits
  - Section 8.1 Supplemental Account Payments (other than death or disability):
    - Rules apply separately to the portion subject to the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election and to any other elected portion.
    - Lump sum: paid on the first January 1 or July 1 at least six months after Separation from Service (other than death or disability), within 90 days.
    - Installments: begin on July 1 of the calendar year after Separation from Service, and continue each July 1, each within 90 days.
    - Rehire after Separation does not change the established payment schedule.
    - If a participant made a one-time permissible change to the initial Supplemental Election (under Sections 5.4(a)(ii) or 5.4(d)) effective before Separation, the affected Supplemental Benefits are delayed by five years from the otherwise applicable payment/commencement date; the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election cannot be modified and is not subject to this five-year delay.
    - Installment calculation uses a declining-balance method: each payment equals the then-remaining Supplemental Benefits multiplied by 1/(number of remaining payments).
    - Payments are limited to the vested portion determined under the Qualified Retirement Plans’ vesting rules; non-vested amounts are forfeited.

  - Section 8.2 Deferral Account Payments (other than death or disability):
    - Post-2010 deferrals generally follow Section 8.1 unless a special payment election under Section 6.5 applies; Pre-2011 deferrals follow Sections 8.2(b)(i) or 8.2(c)(i).
    - Specified Date Elections for Employees in Band 50 or above:
      - If no Separation from Service, death, or Disability by the specified date, Pre-2011 deferrals are paid as elected:
        - Lump sum: on the first March 15 or September 15 after the specified date (or on that date if it is March 15 or September 15), within 90 days.
        - Installments: begin on the first March 15 or September 15 after the specified date (or on that date), and continue each March 15, each within 90 days.

nodes.title: Deferral Account Payments (Other than Payments Due to Death or Disability)
nodes.heading: Section 8.2 Deferral Account Payments (Other than Payments Due to Death or Disability) .
nodes.start_phrase: With respect to Post-2010 Deferral Benefits, payments not made on accoun t of death or Disability will be governed by Section 8.1 except to the extent that a Participant was eligible to make a special payment election with respect to such Deferral Benefits pursuant to Section 6.5, in which case payment will be governed by Section 8.2(b) or Section 8.2(c), as applicable.
nodes.summary:
- Supplemental Benefits (Section 8.1): 
  - If a participant amends an election under 8.1(a), payments (or the start of installments) are delayed five years from the original 8.1(a) date; rehire during this period does not change the schedule.
  - The Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election cannot be modified and is not subject to the five-year delay.
  - Annual installments are paid using a declining-fraction method: each payment equals the then-remaining Supplemental Benefits multiplied by 1 divided by the number of remaining payments.
  - Payments are limited to the vested portion of the Supplemental Account; non-vested amounts are forfeited (vesting per the Qualified Retirement Plans).

- Deferral Account Payments other than for death or disability (Section 8.2):
  - General rule: Post-2010 Deferral Benefits follow Section 8.1 unless a special payment election under 6.5 applies; Pre-2011 Deferral Benefits follow 8.2(b)(i) or 8.2(c)(i).
  - Specified date elections for Employees in Band 50 or above (8.2(b)):
    - Pre-2011: 
      - Lump sum: paid on the first March 15 or September 15 following the specified date (or on that date if chosen), within 90 days.
      - Installments: begin on the first March 15 or September 15 following (or on) the specified date, then each March 15 within 90 days for the elected period.
      - If Separation from Service occurs before all installments are paid: if Retirement Eligible, continue as scheduled; if not, remaining installments convert to a lump sum under 8.2(c)(i).
    - Post-2010:
      - Lump sum: paid on the first January 1 or July 1 coinciding with or following the specified date, within 90 days.
      - Installments: begin on the first January 1 or July 1 coinciding with or following the specified date, then each January 1 or July 1 within 90 days for the elected period.
      - If Separation from Service occurs before completion, remaining installments continue as scheduled.
  - Separation from Service for Employees in Band 50 or above (8.2(c))—applies regardless of any later specified date:
    - Pre-2011:
      - Retirement Eligible: 
        - Lump sum: paid on the first March 15 or September 15 at least six months after separation, within 90 days.
        - Installments: begin on the first March 15 or September 15 at least six months after separation, then each March 15 within 90 days for the elected period.
        - Re-employment does not change the existing schedule.
      - Not Retirement Eligible: all Deferral Benefits are paid in a lump sum on the first March 15 or September 15 at least six months after separation, within 90 days.
    - Post-2010:
      - Lump sum: paid on the first January 1 or July 1 at least six months after separation, within 90 days.
      - Installments: begin on the first July 1 in the calendar year following separation, then each July 1 within 90 days for the elected period.
      - Re-employment does not change the existing schedule.
  - Installment calculation (8.2(d)): declining-fraction method using 1 divided by the number of remaining payments (e.g., 1/5, then 1/4 of the remaining balance, etc.).
  - Payments limited to vested Deferral Account amounts; non-vested amounts are forfeited (8.2(e)).

- Beneficiary designations (Section 8.3): 
  - Participants may separately designate beneficiaries for the Supplemental Account and the Deferral Account, and may revoke/modify at any time via the Administrator’s prescribed form.
  - Designation is automatically revoked upon the beneficiary’s death or, if the beneficiary is the spouse, upon divorce.
  - If no designation is in effect when due, the beneficiary is the surviving spouse; if none, the participant’s estate.

nodes.title: Designation of Beneficiaries
nodes.heading: Section 8.3 Designation of Beneficia ries.
nodes.start_phrase: A Partici pant may separately designate a Beneficiary or Beneficiaries entitled to receive payment of his or her Supplemental Account and his or her Deferral Account by filing written notice of such designation with the Administrat or in such form as the Administrator may prescribe.
nodes.summary:
- Payment timing after Separation from Service:
  - If not Retirement Eligible: all Deferral Benefits are paid in a lump sum on the first March 15 or September 15 at least six months after separation, or as soon as administratively feasible within 90 days.
  - For Post-2010 Deferral Benefits:
    - If a lump sum was elected: payment on the first January 1 or July 1 at least six months after separation, or within 90 days thereafter.
    - If annual installments were elected: first payment on the first July 1 of the calendar year following separation, then each July 1 thereafter for the elected period, each within 90 days as administratively feasible.
  - Re-employment after separation does not change an established payment schedule.

- Installment calculation:
  - Each annual installment equals the current account balance for the elected portion multiplied by 1 divided by the remaining number of payments (e.g., 1/5, then 1/4, etc.).

- Vesting:
  - Distributions are limited to the vested portion of the Deferral Account at the time of payment; any non-vested amounts are forfeited.

- Beneficiary designations:
  - Participants may separately designate beneficiaries for the Supplemental Account and the Deferral Account, and may modify or revoke at any time using prescribed forms.
  - Automatic revocation occurs upon the beneficiary’s death or, if the beneficiary is the spouse, upon dissolution of marriage.
  - Default beneficiary if no designation: surviving spouse, or if none, the participant’s estate.
  - For deaths on or after January 1, 2013: spousal beneficiary designations are automatically void upon divorce, subject to any applicable domestic relations order; participants may re-designate a former spouse after divorce. Similar rules apply where a beneficiary is permitted to designate a beneficiary and later divorces that person.
  - The plan is not liable for payments made to a named beneficiary before the plan is notified of a divorce.

- Death benefits:
  - Supplemental Account:
    - If death occurs while actively employed: lump-sum payment on the first January 1 or July 1 at least six months after death, or within 90 days thereafter.
    - If installments were elected and death occurs after installments began (or during a delay due to a modified election): remaining installments are accelerated and paid as a lump sum on the first January 1 or July 1 at least six months after death, or within 90 days thereafter.
    - If death occurs after separation but before the scheduled payment date (six months after separation): payment is made to the beneficiary on the originally scheduled date. Any five-year delay due to a modified election is disregarded upon death; death benefit rules apply immediately.
  - Deferral Account (Pre-2011 Deferral Benefits):
    - If death occurs while actively employed: lump-sum payment on the first March 15 or September 15 at least six months after death, or within 90 days thereafter.
    - If installments were elected and death occurs after installments began: remaining installments are accelerated and paid as a lump sum on the first March 15 or September 15 at least six months after death, or within 90 days thereafter.

nodes.title: Death
nodes.heading: Section 8.4 Death .
nodes.start_phrase: Upon a Participant’ s death, payment of the Participant’ s Supplemental Account shall be made to the Participant’ s Beneficiary or Beneficiaries designated to receive the Participant’ s Supplemental Account.
nodes.summary:
- Automatic revocation of spousal beneficiary upon divorce (effective for deaths on/after Jan 1, 2013): any spouse designation for either/both Accounts becomes void at divorce, subject to rights under a domestic relations order; benefits then paid as if former spouse predeceased the Participant. A former spouse can be re‑named via a new post‑divorce designation. Same rules apply when a beneficiary who is allowed to designate a beneficiary divorces. The Plan is not liable for payments made to a named beneficiary before it is notified of the divorce.
- Death benefits — Supplemental Account (Section 8.4(a)):
  - Paid to designated beneficiary(ies).
  - If death occurs while actively employed: paid as a single lump sum on the first Jan 1 or Jul 1 at least six months after death (or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but no later than 90 days).
  - If installments were elected and death occurs after installments begin (or while awaiting installment start due to a post‑separation modification): remaining installments are converted to a single lump sum on the first Jan 1 or Jul 1 at least six months after death (same 90‑day outer limit).
  - If death occurs after Separation from Service but before the scheduled Jan 1/Jul 1 payment date that is six months post‑separation, payment is made on the originally scheduled date.
  - If a five‑year payment delay applied due to a modification of a Supplemental Election, death benefits are paid under these death rules without waiting for the five‑year period.
- Death benefits — Deferral Account (Section 8.4(b)):
  - Paid to designated beneficiary(ies).
  - Pre‑2011 Deferral Benefits:
    - If death while actively employed: single lump sum on the first Mar 15 or Sep 15 at least six months after death (or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but no later than 90 days).
    - If installments were elected and death occurs after installments begin: remaining installments paid as a single lump sum on the first Mar 15 or Sep 15 at least six months after death (same 90‑day outer limit).
    - If death occurs after Separation from Service but before the scheduled Mar 15/Sep 15 date that is six months post‑separation, payment is made on the originally scheduled date.
  - Post‑2010 Deferral Benefits:
    - If death while actively employed: single lump sum on the first Jan 1 or Jul 1 at least six months after death (or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but no later than 90 days).
    - If installments were elected and death occurs after installments begin (or while awaiting start due to a modification): remaining installments paid as a single lump sum on the first Jan 1 or Jul 1 at least six months after death (same 90‑day limit).
    - If death occurs after Separation from Service but before the scheduled Jan 1/Jul 1 date that is six months post‑separation, payment is made on the originally scheduled date.
    - If a five‑year delay applied due to a modification of a Supplemental Election that also applies to Deferral Benefits, death benefits are paid under these death rules without waiting five years.
- Disability — Supplemental Account (Section 8.5(a)):
  - Rules applied separately to amounts under the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election and any differing elected amounts.
  - If lump sum was elected: paid on the first Jan 1 or Jul 1 at least six months after the Disability date (or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but no later than 90 days).
  - If installments were elected: payments begin on Jul 1 of the calendar year following Disability (or as soon thereafter as administratively feasible, but no later than 90 days) and continue each Jul 1 for the elected period.
- Disability — Deferral Accounts (Section 8.5(b)): section begins but details are not included in this excerpt.

nodes.title: Disability
nodes.heading: Section 8.5 Disability .
nodes.start_phrase: By way of clarification, the rules set forth in this Section shall be applied separately to the portion of the Participant’ s Supplem ental Benefits that is subject to the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election and the remainder of the Participant’ s Supplemental Benefits that is not covered by the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election, to the extent that the Participant’ s Supplemental Election differs from the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election.
nodes.summary:
- Death benefits and timing rules:
  - For Post-2010 Deferral Benefits, if a participant dies while employed, the account is paid in a single lump sum on the first January 1 or July 1 at least six months after death (or as soon as administratively feasible, but no later than 90 days).
  - If a participant elected installments and dies before or after installments begin, remaining amounts are paid to the beneficiary as a lump sum on the first January 1 or July 1 at least six months after death (within the 90-day administrative window).
  - If death occurs after Separation from Service but before the scheduled six-month payment date, the lump sum is paid to the beneficiary on the originally scheduled date (or within 90 days).
  - Any prior five-year payment delay due to a modified Supplemental Election is overridden upon death; death benefit provisions control.

- Disability benefits (Section 8.5):
  - Rules apply separately to portions of Supplemental Benefits subject to the Automatic New Participant Supplemental Election and any differing participant elections.
  - Supplemental Account:
    - Lump sum: paid on the first January 1 or July 1 at least six months after disability (within 90 days).
    - Installments: begin July 1 of the calendar year following disability and continue each July 1 (each within 90 days).
  - Deferral Accounts:
    - Pre-2011 Deferral Benefits:
      - Lump sum: first March 15 or September 15 at least six months after disability (within 90 days).
      - Installments: begin the first March 15 or September 15 at least six months after disability and continue each March 15 (each within 90 days).
    - Post-2010 Deferral Benefits:
      - Lump sum: first January 1 or July 1 at least six months after disability (within 90 days).
      - Installments: begin July 1 of the calendar year following disability and continue each July 1 (each within 90 days).

- Unforeseeable Emergency withdrawals (Section 8.6):
  - Participant may request a partial or full payout limited to the lesser of the vested Account balance or the amount necessary to satisfy the emergency plus anticipated taxes/penalties.
  - No payout if the need can be met by insurance/reimbursement, asset liquidation (without severe hardship), or stopping deferrals.
  - Upon approval, payment is a lump sum on the approval date or as soon as feasible, but no later than 90 days.
  - Administrator decides how the payment is allocated across accounts/subaccounts, consistent with Section 409A.

- Company offset (Section 8.7):
  - To the maximum extent permitted by Section 409A and applicable law, amounts otherwise payable may be forfeited or payments suspended to satisfy Company claims, including enforcement of detrimental conduct provisions, recovery of debts, or benefit overpayments.

nodes.title: Unforeseeable Emergency
nodes.heading: Section 8.6 Unfor eseeable Emergency .
nodes.start_phrase: If a Participant experiences an Unforeseeable Emer gency , the Participant may petition the Administrator to receive a partial or full payout from the Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Disability distribution timing:
  - Pre-2011 deferrals: 
    - Lump sum paid on the first March 15 or September 15 at least six months after disability (or as soon as administratively feasible, but no later than 90 days).
    - Installments begin on the first March 15 or September 15 at least six months after disability (or as soon feasible, but no later than 90 days) and continue each March 15 for the elected period (same 90-day administrative window).
  - Post-2010 deferrals:
    - Lump sum paid on the first January 1 or July 1 at least six months after disability (or as soon feasible, but no later than 90 days).
    - Installments begin on July 1 of the calendar year following disability (or as soon feasible, but no later than 90 days) and continue each July 1 for the elected period (same 90-day window).

- Unforeseeable Emergency withdrawals (Section 8.6):
  - Participant may petition for a payout limited to the lesser of the vested account balance or the amount necessary to satisfy the emergency plus anticipated taxes/penalties.
  - Not available if the emergency can be alleviated by insurance/other compensation, liquidation of assets that wouldn’t itself cause severe hardship, or by ceasing deferrals.
  - If approved, paid in a lump sum on approval or as soon as administratively feasible, but no later than 90 days.
  - Administrator decides, consistent with Section 409A, how payments are applied across the participant’s account and subaccounts.

- Company offset/clawback (Section 8.7):
  - To the maximum extent permitted by Section 409A and applicable law, amounts otherwise payable may be forfeited or suspended to satisfy Company claims.
  - Includes enforcement of detrimental conduct provisions under the long-term incentive plan, recovery of debts to the Company, or recovery of benefit overpayments.
  - Applies notwithstanding any contrary terms in the Plan, RP, or RSP.

nodes.title: Company Offset
nodes.heading: Section 8.7 Company Offset .
nodes.start_phrase: Notwiths tanding anything in the Plan, the RP or the RSP to the contrary , to the maximum extent permitted by Section 409A and applicable law, any amount otherwise due or payable under the Plan may be forfeited, or its payment suspended, at the discretion of the Administrator , to apply toward or recover any claim the Company may have against the Participant, including but not limited to, for the enforcement of Amex’ s Detrimental Conduct provisions under its long-term incentive award plan, to recover a debt to the Company or to recover a benefit overpayment under a Company benefit plan or program.
nodes.summary:
- Disability distributions: Specifies payment timing for Deferral Benefits upon a Participant’s Disability, distinguishing between Pre-2011 and Post-2010 deferrals and between lump-sum and installment elections. Pre-2011 payouts occur on the first March 15 or September 15 at least six months after Disability (with a “no later than 90 days” administrative window). Post-2010 lump sums occur on the first January 1 or July 1 at least six months after Disability; Post-2010 installments begin July 1 of the calendar year following Disability and continue annually, each subject to the same administrative window.
- Unforeseeable Emergency withdrawals: Participants may petition for a lump-sum distribution limited to the lesser of the vested Account balance or the amount necessary to satisfy the emergency plus expected taxes/penalties. No payout if the need can be met by insurance, non-hardship asset liquidation, or stopping deferrals. Administrator has sole discretion; payment is made promptly but no later than 90 days, with allocation across subaccounts determined consistent with Section 409A.
- Company offset/clawback: To the extent permitted by Section 409A and applicable law, the Administrator may forfeit or suspend plan payments to satisfy Company claims (e.g., enforcement of Amex detrimental conduct provisions, debts, or benefit overpayments), with offsets only when amounts would otherwise be distributable and in accordance with the Company’s Section 409A policy.
- Tax withholding: The Company may withhold required income and employment taxes from any payment or require the Participant to pay such taxes in advance, subject to Section 409A.
- De minimis cash-out: The Administrator may mandate a lump-sum payout of small balances equal to the Account’s lump-sum value, not exceeding the Code Section 402(g)(1)(B) limit, provided it liquidates the Participant’s entire interest in this and all similar account balance arrangements under Treas. Reg. 1.409A-1(c)(2).
- Change in Control (partial definition): Defines a Change in Control, in part, as a Person acquiring 25% or more of Amex’s outstanding common shares or voting securities, with exceptions for acquisitions by Amex, its subsidiaries, employee benefit plans, underwriters, certain 13G filers (until switching to 13D), and some reorganization/merger scenarios (definition continues beyond the excerpt).

nodes.title: Withholding
nodes.heading: Section 8.8 Withholding .
nodes.start_phrase: The Company shall be entitled to deduct from any payment under the Plan, regardless of the form of such payment, the amount of all applicable income and employment taxes, if any, required by law to be withheld with respect to such payment or may require the Participant to pay to it such tax prior to and, to the extent permissible under Section 409A, as a condition of the making of such payment.
nodes.summary:
- Offsets against a participant’s account: Amounts owed can be offset against a participant’s account balance before distribution, but only to the extent and in the manner allowed under Section 409A and the plan’s Section 409A Policy.
- Tax withholding: The company may deduct required income and employment taxes from any plan payment or require the participant to pay such taxes beforehand, consistent with Section 409A.
- De minimis lump-sum cashout: The administrator may mandatorily cash out a participant’s entire account in a lump sum equal to its value if (1) it fully terminates and liquidates the participant’s interests under this plan and all similar account balance plans under Treas. Reg. §1.409A-1(c)(2), and (2) the amount does not exceed the Code §402(g)(1)(B) limit.
- Change in Control definition: A Change in Control includes when a person or group acquires 25% or more of Amex’s outstanding common shares or voting power, subject to exclusions for certain acquisitions (e.g., by Amex or its subsidiaries, employee benefit plans, underwriters in offerings, certain 13G filers until 13D filing is required, and specified reorganizations/mergers/consolidations). The excerpt indicates additional details continue beyond the provided text.

nodes.title: De Minimis Lump Sum Payment
nodes.heading: Section 8.9 De Minimis Lump Sum Payment .
nodes.start_phrase: Notwithstanding the other provisions of the Plan, the Administrator may, in its sole discretion, make a mandatory lump sum pay-out of a Participant’ s Account at any time, provided that such pay-out amount shall be in an amount equal to the lump sum value of such Account determine d for the date of such pay-out; and further provided that such pay-out (1) accompanies the termination and liquidation of the Participant’ s entire interest under the Plan and all similar arrangements that constitute an account balance plan under Section 1.409A-1(c) (2) of the Treasury Regulations; and (2) the payment is not greater than the applicable dollar amount under Section 402(g)(1)(B) of the Code.
nodes.summary:
- Offset of amounts: The company may offset amounts from a participant’s account before they would otherwise be distributed to satisfy obligations, but only to the extent and in the manner permitted under the plan’s Section 409A policy.
- Tax withholding: The company can withhold required income and employment taxes from any plan payment, or require the participant to pay such taxes in advance as a condition of payment, to the extent permitted by Section 409A.
- De minimis lump-sum cashout: The administrator may require a lump-sum payout equal to the account’s lump-sum value at any time, provided it fully terminates the participant’s interest under this plan and all similar account balance arrangements under Treas. Reg. §1.409A-1(c)(2), and the payment does not exceed the Code §402(g)(1)(B) limit.
- Change in Control (partial definition): A Change in Control includes a person becoming the beneficial owner of 25% or more of Amex’s outstanding common shares or voting power, measured under Exchange Act Rules (Sections 13(d), 14(d), Rule 13d-3), with exclusions for acquisitions by Amex or its subsidiaries, employee benefit plans, temporary underwriter holdings, certain Schedule 13G filers until they file on Schedule 13D, and certain reorganizations/mergers (definition continues).

nodes.title: CHANGE IN CONTROL
nodes.heading: ARTICLE 9 CHANGE IN CONTROL
nodes.start_phrase: “Change in Control ” means the happening of any of the following:
nodes.summary:
- Offsets: Amounts owed may be offset against a participant’s account before distribution, but only to the extent and in the manner allowed under Section 409A and the plan’s Section 409A Policy.
- Tax withholding: The company may withhold required income and employment taxes from any plan payment, or require the participant to pay such taxes in advance, subject to Section 409A.
- De minimis lump-sum payout: The administrator may, in its discretion, require a lump-sum cash-out equal to the account’s lump-sum value at the payout date if it fully terminates and liquidates the participant’s interest under this and all similar account-balance plans (Treas. Reg. 1.409A-1(c)(2)) and the payment does not exceed the Code §402(g)(1)(B) limit.
- Change in Control (Article 9): Defines a Change in Control of Amex, including when a person becomes the beneficial owner (under Exchange Act Rule 13d-3) of 25% or more of outstanding common shares or voting power, with exceptions for acquisitions by Amex or its subsidiaries, employee benefit plans, temporary underwriters, certain passive 13G filers (until 13D filing, which resets the deemed acquisition date), and certain reorganizations/mergers/consolidations (details continue beyond the excerpt).

nodes.title: Change in Control
nodes.heading: Section 9.1 Change in Contr ol.
nodes.start_phrase: “Change in Control ” means the happening of any of the following:
nodes.summary:
- Offsets: Amounts may be offset against a participant’s account before distribution, but only to the extent and in the manner permitted under Section 409A and the plan’s Section 409A policy.
- Tax withholding: The Company may withhold required income and employment taxes from any plan payment or require the participant to pay such taxes as a condition of payment, consistent with Section 409A.
- De minimis lump-sum payout: The Administrator may mandate a lump-sum cashout equal to the account’s lump-sum value if (1) it fully terminates the participant’s interest under this plan and all similar account balance arrangements, and (2) the payment does not exceed the Code §402(g)(1)(B) dollar limit.

- Article 9—Change in Control (CIC) definition:
  - 25% ownership trigger: A CIC occurs if a Person becomes the beneficial owner of 25% or more of Amex’s outstanding common shares or voting power, with detailed exceptions (e.g., acquisitions by Amex, subsidiaries, employee benefit plans, underwriters, certain Schedule 13G reporters, and qualifying reorganizations). Includes an anti-dilution “creeper” rule addressing effects of Amex share repurchases.
  - Board turnover: A CIC occurs if the Incumbent Board ceases to constitute a majority of the Board, excluding changes arising from contested elections or proxy solicitations.
  - Business Combination: Certain mergers, consolidations, share exchanges, or similar transactions constitute a CIC unless post-transaction (i) prior holders retain >50% of common stock/voting power, (ii) no Person holds ≥25%, and (iii) a majority of the resulting board were Incumbent Board members.
  - Asset sale: A sale, lease, exchange, or disposition of all or substantially all assets constitutes a CIC unless similar post-transaction continuity tests are met.
  - Liquidation/dissolution: Shareholder approval of a complete liquidation or dissolution is a CIC.

- Effect of a Change in Control:
  - Rabbi Trust funding: Upon a CIC, to the extent permitted by Section 409A, the Company must fund a trust with the full value of each participant’s account.
  - Account earnings: Special rules apply to earnings crediting for RSP-related accounts effective upon a CIC (details continue beyond the excerpt).

nodes.title: Effect of Change in Control
nodes.heading: Section 9.2 Effect of Change in Contr ol.
nodes.start_phrase: This Section 9.2 shall apply in the event of a Change in Control.
nodes.summary:
- Defines additional Change in Control triggers and exceptions for Amex:
  - Certain business combinations count only if post-transaction board and ownership thresholds aren’t met; safe harbors if a majority of the resulting board are Incumbent Board members and prior shareholders retain specified ownership/voting levels, with limits on any 25%+ new owner.
  - Sale, lease, exchange, or disposition of all or substantially all assets may be a Change in Control unless continuity of ownership, voting power, and board majority of Incumbent Board members is maintained and no new 25%+ owner emerges.
  - Shareholder approval of a complete liquidation or dissolution is a Change in Control.
- Effect of a Change in Control (Section 9.2):
  - Rabbi Trust funding: To the extent permitted under Section 409A, all Participants’ Plan Accounts are fully funded and maintained in a trust immediately upon a Change in Control.
  - Account earnings adjustments:
    - RSP-Related Accounts:
      - Subaccounts tied to the Stock Fund switch to the Stable Value Fund after a Change in Control.
      - If the RSP is frozen/terminated without a comparable replacement or has no available investment options, credit at least the Applicable Federal Rate (AFR).
    - Deferral Accounts:
      - Interest Method: Minimum Schedule Rate is no less than Moody’s A Rate for the year of the Change in Control and thereafter; for Executive Officers, the rate is capped at AFR if ROE is Below Target Range.
      - Hypothetical Investment Method: Treated like RSP-Related Accounts (shift to Stable Value/AFR floor as applicable).
      - Vesting: Certain participants who separate within two years post-Change in Control and who would have become Retirement Eligible during the normal severance period become 100% vested in earnings under Section 7.5(b)(i).
  - Golden Parachute excise tax (Sections 280G/4999) cutback:
    - Payments are reduced, if necessary, to avoid Excise Tax only when such reduction increases (or at least does not decrease) the participant’s net after-tax amount; participants may elect the order of reductions among their Total Payments.
    - “Total Payments” broadly includes all payments/benefits connected to the Change in Control or termination; determinations (what counts as parachute payments, reasonable compensation, valuations) are made by the Company’s pre-Change in Control auditor or another designated qualified firm, using highest marginal tax rate assumptions.
    - Company must provide affected participants a written calculation and basis (with attached opinions) within 30 days after the Change in Control.
- Claims Procedures (Article 10) begin:
  - Introduces process for a claimant to file a claim if benefits are denied or if the claimant has another Plan-related claim.

nodes.title: CLAIMS PROCEDURES
nodes.heading: ARTICLE 10 CLAIMS PROCEDURES
nodes.start_phrase: A claimant who believes that he or she is being denied Benefits to which he or she is entitled under the Plan or who otherwise has a claim involving the Plan may file a written request for such Benefits or written description of the claim (as applicable) with the Administrator , setting forth his or her claim for Benefits or other claim involving the Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Outlines how to determine whether change-in-control-related payments are subject to the Section 4999 excise tax and whether they must be reduced:
  - “Total Payments” include all payments/benefits connected to a change in control or employment termination under this plan or any other arrangement with the company, the change-in-control party, or affiliates, and are treated as parachute payments unless the designated accounting firm concludes otherwise under Section 280G.
  - Amounts the participant validly waives so they do not constitute “payments” under Section 280G(b) are excluded.
  - Excess parachute payments are presumed subject to the excise tax unless the firm determines they represent reasonable compensation above the base amount or are otherwise exempt.
  - The firm determines the value of non-cash and deferred benefits per Section 280G(d)(3)-(4).
  - Tax assumptions for reduction analyses use the participant’s highest marginal federal and state/local rates (net of deductibility of state/local taxes).
  - The “Firm” is the company’s independent auditor immediately before the change in control, or another qualified firm designated by the committee if the auditor declines; the company pays the firm’s reasonable fees.
- Requires the company, within 30 days after a change in control, to deliver to any participant whose payments are proposed to be reduced a written statement explaining the Total Payments calculation and its basis, with attached written opinions/advice from the firm or other advisors.
- Begins Article 10 (Claims Procedures), stating that a claimant who believes they are being denied plan benefits or otherwise has a plan-related claim may file a claim (procedure details to follow).

nodes.title: CLAIMS PROCEDURES - Introduction
nodes.heading: ARTICLE 10 CLAIMS PROCEDURES
nodes.start_phrase: A claimant who believes that he or she is being denied Benefits to which he or she is entitled under the Plan or who otherwise has a claim involving the Plan may file a written request for such Benefits or written description of the claim (as applicable) with the Administrator , setting forth his or her claim for Benefits or other claim involving the Plan.
