nodes.title: Claim
nodes.heading: Section 10.1 Claim .
nodes.start_phrase: A claimant who believes that he or she is being denied Benefits to which he or she is entitled under the Plan or who otherwise has a claim involving the Plan may file a written request for such Benefits or written description of the claim (as applicable) with the Administrator , setting forth his or her claim for Benefits or other claim involving the Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Change in Control excise tax (Section 280G) framework and potential payment “cutback”:
  - Defines “Total Payments” to include all compensation/benefits tied to a Change in Control or termination from the company or related parties.
  - Presumes all such amounts are parachute payments unless the designated accounting firm (the company’s pre-CIC independent auditor or another qualified firm selected by the Committee) opines otherwise, including via Code Section 280G exceptions.
  - Excludes amounts the participant validly waives so they are not “payments” under 280G.
  - Treats excess parachute payments as subject to the 4999 excise tax unless the firm determines they are reasonable compensation above the base amount or otherwise exempt.
  - Requires valuation of non-cash and deferred benefits per 280G(d)(3)-(4) principles.
  - Uses highest marginal federal, state, and local income tax rates (net of federal deductibility of state/local taxes) to model net benefit when determining any reduction.
  - The firm’s fees are paid by the company.

- Participant disclosure after a Change in Control:
  - Within 30 days post-CIC, if any participant’s payments are proposed to be reduced, the company must provide a written statement detailing Total Payments calculations, the methodology, and attach any written opinions/advice from the firm or other advisors.

- Article 10 Claims Procedures:
  - How to file a claim for benefits or other plan-related claims: written submission to the Administrator.
  - Limitations period: no action may be brought after the earlier of 90 days following final appeal denial or one year from claim accrual. Accrual occurs when the claimant knew or should have known the plan clearly repudiated the claim/position. The Administrator is the plan’s agent for service of process.
  - Exhaustion requirement: claimants must exhaust plan remedies before seeking relief under Section 10.5.

- Claim decision timelines and content of denials:
  - Standard claims: Administrator responds within 90 days; may extend once for 90 days with advance notice and reason.
  - Denial notices must include: specific reasons, plan provisions relied upon, information needed to perfect the claim and why, steps for review (including right to access relevant documents), time limits for review (Sections 10.3 and 10.4), and the right to bring an ERISA Section 502 action (subject to Section 10.5).

- Disability-related claims (when the Administrator makes the disability determination for plan benefits):
  - Decision within 45 days, with up to two 30-day extensions for circumstances beyond the plan’s control, with advance written notice for each extension.

nodes.title: Claim Decision
nodes.heading: Section 10.2 Claim Decision .
nodes.start_phrase: (a) Except as otherwise provided by Section 10.2(b), the Administrator shall reply to any claim filed under Section 10.1 within 90 days of receipt, unless it determines to extend such reply period for an additional 90 days for reasonable cause and notifies the claimant in advance of the reasons for the extension and the date by which the Administrator expects to make a decision.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes how to file a claim: a written request/description must be submitted to the Administrator; all plan remedies must be exhausted before seeking judicial relief (Section 10.5).
- Sets strict limitation periods for lawsuits: no action may be brought after the earlier of 90 days from final appeal denial or one year from when the cause of action accrued; accrual occurs when the claimant knew or should have known the Plan clearly repudiated the claim/position. The Administrator is the Plan’s agent for service of process.
- Details standard claim decision timelines and denial content: Administrator responds within 90 days (extendable once for 90 days with advance notice and reasons). Denial notices must explain reasons, cite Plan provisions, identify additional needed information and why, outline review steps and document-access rights, state appeal time limits, and note the right to bring an ERISA §502 action (subject to Section 10.5).
- Provides special rules for disability-related claims decided by the Administrator: decision within 45 days, with up to two 30‑day extensions for circumstances beyond the Plan’s control and advance notices explaining reasons, standards, unresolved issues, and needed information. If more information is required, the claimant gets at least 45 days to provide it, and decision deadlines are tolled.
- Requires enhanced content in disability claim denials: discussion of the decision, including reasons for disagreeing with treating providers, vocational experts, other experts consulted (whether or not relied upon), and any SSA disability determinations; copies of or statements about internal rules/guidelines; and explanations of medical necessity/experimental treatment exclusions (or a statement they will be provided on request).
- Outlines appeal (review) rights and deadlines: standard claims—60 days to request review; disability claims—180 days. Claimants (or representatives) may review relevant documents and submit written comments; relevant documents are provided free of charge (subject to applicable privileges unless ERISA requires otherwise). Failure to timely request review bars further challenge.
- States that, upon review, the Administrator will consider all submitted materials and issue a written decision with specific reasons.

nodes.title: Request for Review
nodes.heading: Section 10.3 Request for Review .
nodes.start_phrase: (a) Except as otherwise provided by Section 10.3(b), within 60 days after the receipt by the claimant of the written explanation described above, the claimant may request in writing that the Administrator review its determination.
nodes.summary:
- Outlines claim processing for benefits, especially disability-related claims, including when the Administrator may extend decision deadlines and what must be included in extension notices (reasons, expected decision date, benefit standards, unresolved issues, and required additional information).
- Provides that, for disability claims needing more information, claimants get at least 45 days to submit it, during which notice and decision deadlines are tolled.
- Specifies enhanced content requirements for disability claim denial notices: detailed discussion of the decision; explanations for disagreeing with treating and vocational professionals’ views; disclosure of medical/vocational expert opinions obtained by the Plan (whether relied upon or not); consideration of any Social Security disability determinations; provision of internal rules/guidelines relied upon or a statement that none exist; and, if a medical necessity/experimental treatment exclusion applies, an explanation of the scientific/clinical judgment or a statement it will be provided free upon request.
- Sets appeal (request for review) rights and deadlines: 60 days for most claims; 180 days for disability claims. Failure to timely request review bars further challenges.
- Affords claimants (or authorized representatives) the right to review relevant documents and submit written issues/comments; relevant documents are available free of charge upon request, subject to attorney-client/work-product and other privileges unless ERISA requires otherwise.
- States that on review, the Administrator will consider all materials and issue a written decision with specific reasons.

nodes.title: Review of Decision
nodes.heading: Section 10.4 Review of Decision .
nodes.start_phrase: (a) After conside ring all materials presented by the claimant, the Adminis trator will render a written decision, setting forth the specific reasons for the decision and containing specific references to the relevant provisions of the Plan on which the decision is based.
nodes.summary:
- Explains claim processing extensions and required contents of extension notices, including reasons for delay, expected decision date, standards for benefit entitlement, unresolved issues, and additional information needed; for disability-status claims, claimants get at least 45 days to supply additional information, and all decision deadlines are tolled during that period.
- Details the required content of written denials for disability-related claims: a discussion explaining the basis for disagreement with treating providers, vocational evaluators, consulting experts, and any Social Security disability determination; disclosure or confirmation of the absence of internal rules/guidelines relied on; and the scientific/clinical rationale for medical-necessity or experimental-treatment limits (or a statement that it will be provided free upon request).
- Sets appeal (request for review) timelines and rights:
  - General claims: 60 days to request review; right to review and receive, free of charge, relevant documents, subject to attorney-client, work-product, and other privileges unless ERISA requires otherwise; failure to timely appeal bars further challenge.
  - Disability-status claims: 180 days to request review; same access rights; failure to timely appeal bars further challenge.
- Describes the appeal decision process and timing:
  - Written decision in plain language with specific reasons and Plan provisions cited; normally within 60 days, extendable to 120 days with notice; deadlines tolled while claimant supplies requested information.
  - Decision must inform claimant of the right to access relevant documents free of charge and the right to bring an ERISA Section 502 action; for disability-status decisions, must also state the applicable limitations period and the calendar date it expires.
- Imposes additional protections for disability-status appeals:
  - No deference to the initial determination; reviewers must be different individuals and not subordinates of original decision-makers.
  - No new evidence or rationales may be used without first providing them to the claimant free of charge, sufficiently in advance to allow a response.
  - Required consultation with appropriately trained/experienced health care professionals; identification of any medical/vocational experts consulted; no overlap with initial determination consultants or their subordinates.
  - Decision due within 45 days (extendable to 90 days for special circumstances with notice), with tolling while claimant provides requested information.
  - Denial notice must include the same enhanced explanations, internal-rule disclosures, and scientific/clinical rationale as at the initial denial stage.
- States that all decisions on review are final and binding to the maximum extent permitted by law.
- Establishes a binding arbitration framework after exhaustion of internal claims:
  - Either the Administrator or claimant may compel arbitration for Plan-related claims, except disability-status determinations (unless the participant consents) and any claims where mandatory arbitration is prohibited and the claimant does not consent.
  - Exhaustion of administrative remedies is required even if a claim is initiated outside the process.
  - Arbitration procedures follow the governing Policy to the extent consistent with the Plan, including a prohibition on class or representative proceedings; participants and others waive class/representative rights in arbitration and class actions, subject to preservation of non-waivable statutory rights and remedies.
  - If a non-waivable remedy cannot be granted in arbitration, it may be sought in court.
  - The arbitrator is bound by the Plan and ERISA, applying ERISA’s standard of review that defers to the Administrator’s factual findings and Plan interpretations unless arbitrary and capricious.

nodes.title: Arbitration
nodes.heading: Section 10.5 Arbitration .
nodes.start_phrase: Notwiths tanding anything herein to the contrary , and except with respect to a claim which requires the Adminis trator to make a determination with respect to the Participant’ s disabled status (unless the Participant consents to binding arbitration of such claim) or any other claim as to which mandatory arbitration is prohibited by law and the claimant does not consent to arbitr ation, upon completion of the claims process set forth in this Article 10, the Administrator or a claimant will have the right to compel binding arbitration with respect to any claim involving the Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Outlines what the Administrator must provide with an adverse benefit decision on review: a detailed discussion explaining disagreements with the claimant’s treating health care and vocational professionals, any Plan-retained medical/vocational experts (whether or not relied upon), and any Social Security disability determinations; copies of any internal rules, guidelines, or protocols relied upon (or a statement that none exist); and the scientific or clinical rationale for medical-necessity/experimental-treatment exclusions (or notice that such rationale is available free upon request).
- States that decisions on review are final and binding to the maximum extent permitted by law.
- Establishes a post-exhaustion right for either party to compel binding arbitration for any Plan-related claim, except for disability-status determinations without the participant’s consent and claims where mandatory arbitration is legally prohibited absent consent.
- Provides that arbitration follows the governing Policy to the extent consistent with the Plan, including a prohibition on class or representative proceedings; all claimants and participants waive class/representative actions in arbitration, while preserving non-waivable statutory rights and allowing court recourse for remedies that cannot legally be arbitrated.
- Requires the arbitrator to apply the Plan and ERISA, using the ERISA standard of review that defers to the Administrator’s factual findings and Plan interpretations unless arbitrary and capricious.

nodes.title: Burden of Proof
nodes.heading: Section 10.6 Burd en of Proof.
nodes.start_phrase: Notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary , to the extent a claimant assert s entitlement to Benefits or otherwise makes a claim based upon facts not contained in the Plan’s records, such person shall be required to provide satisfactory affirmative evidence of such facts.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes claimant burden of proof: anyone asserting benefits based on facts not in the Plan’s records (including service or compensation such as Base Salary, Incentive Pay, or RSP/RP-related amounts) must provide satisfactory affirmative evidence, with the Administrator having sole discretion to determine sufficiency.
- Confers the Administrator exclusive authority over all matters under Article 10; the Committee has no authority and cannot interfere.
- Allows the Committee (or its delegate) to amend or terminate the Plan, but not to reduce benefits already in pay status and not in any manner that would violate Section 409A; definitions of Base Salary or Incentive Pay cannot be amended to impermissibly alter existing deferral elections.
- Describes effects of termination: no further deferrals or contributions; accounts paid under Article 8; the Committee may distribute existing balances at or after termination, ending further obligations, only as permitted by Section 409A.
- States the Plan’s unfunded status: no trust or fiduciary relationship is created; deferred amounts remain part of the Company’s general assets, and participants’ rights are limited accordingly (i.e., akin to general unsecured creditors).

nodes.title: Administrator’s Sole Authority
nodes.heading: Section 10.7 Administrator ’s Sole Authority .
nodes.start_phrase: Notwithstanding Section 3.2 or any other provision of the Plan, the Administrator shall have the sole and exclusive authority with respect to any matter, action or decision under this Article 10, and the Committee shall have neither any authority with respect to such matters, nor the right or ability to limit or to interfere in any way with the Administrator ’s authority with respect to such matters.
nodes.summary:
- Burden of Proof: Claimants must provide satisfactory affirmative evidence for any benefits claim based on facts not in the Plan’s records, including claims tied to service or compensation (e.g., Base Salary, Incentive Pay, RSP/RP-Related Account purposes). The Administrator has sole discretion to decide if the evidence is satisfactory.
- Administrator’s Sole Authority (Article 10): The Administrator exclusively controls all matters, actions, and decisions under Article 10. The Committee has no authority and cannot limit or interfere with the Administrator’s authority for these matters.
- Plan Amendment and Termination:
  - Amendments: The Committee (or delegate) may amend or terminate the Plan at any time but cannot reduce or modify benefits already being paid to Participants or Beneficiaries. Amendments must comply with Section 409A; definitions of Base Salary or Incentive Pay cannot be changed in a way that impermissibly alters existing deferral elections.
  - Effect of Termination: Upon termination, no further deferrals or contributions will be credited. Accounts are paid as provided in Article 8, but the Committee may choose to distribute existing balances at or after termination, with no further obligations thereafter, subject to Section 409A compliance.
- Unfunded Status: The Plan does not create a trust or fiduciary relationship; deferred amounts remain part of the Company’s general funds, and participants’ right to payment is a contractual claim against the Company.

nodes.title: AMENDMENT & TERMINATION
nodes.heading: ARTICLE 1 1 AMENDMENT & TERMINA TION
nodes.start_phrase: The Com mittee or its delegate may, at any time, amend or terminate the Plan, provided that the Committee may not reduce or modify the amount of any Benefit payable to a Participant or any Beneficiary receiving Benefit payments at the time the Plan is amended or terminated.
nodes.summary:
- Burden of Proof (Section 10.6): Claimants must provide satisfactory affirmative evidence for any facts not reflected in the Plan’s records, including service or compensation (e.g., Base Salary, Incentive Pay, RSP-/RP-Related Account amounts). The Administrator has sole discretion to determine whether the evidence is satisfactory.

- Administrator’s Sole Authority (Section 10.7): For all matters under Article 10, the Administrator has exclusive authority; the Committee has no authority and cannot limit or interfere.

- Amendment & Termination (Article 11):
  - Plan Amendment (Section 11.1): The Committee (or delegate) may amend or terminate the Plan at any time, but cannot reduce/modify benefits currently being paid. All amendments must comply with Section 409A; changes to Base Salary or Incentive Pay definitions cannot impermissibly alter existing deferral elections.
  - Effect of Plan Termination (Section 11.2): Upon termination, no new deferrals/contributions are allowed; accounts are paid per Article 8. The Committee may distribute existing account balances at or after termination, ending further obligations, but only in compliance with Section 409A.

- General Provisions—Unfunded Status (Section 12.1): The Plan creates no trust or fiduciary relationship; deferred amounts remain general assets of the Company, and participants’ rights to payment are as unsecured claims against the Company.

nodes.title: Plan Amendment
nodes.heading: Section 11.1 Plan Amendment .
nodes.start_phrase: The Com mittee or its delegate may, at any time, amend or terminate the Plan, provided that the Committee may not reduce or modify the amount of any Benefit payable to a Participant or any Beneficiary receiving Benefit payments at the time the Plan is amended or terminated.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes claimant’s burden of proof: anyone asserting benefits based on facts not in the Plan’s records (e.g., service, Base Salary, Incentive Pay, compensation for RSP- or RP-Related Account purposes) must provide satisfactory affirmative evidence, with the Administrator having sole discretion to determine sufficiency.
- Confirms Administrator’s exclusive authority over all matters under Article 10; the Committee has no authority or ability to interfere in these decisions.
- Provides amendment and termination rules: the Committee (or delegate) may amend or terminate the Plan at any time, but may not reduce or modify benefits already being paid; all changes must comply with Section 409A, and definitions of Base Salary or Incentive Pay cannot be amended in a way that impermissibly alters existing deferral elections.
- Describes effects of Plan termination: no further deferrals or contributions; accounts paid as provided under Article 8; the Committee may distribute existing account balances at or after termination, ending further obligations, subject to Section 409A compliance.
- States the Plan’s unfunded status: no trust or fiduciary relationship is created; deferred amounts remain part of the Company’s general assets and benefits are unsecured promises to pay (section text truncated).

nodes.title: Effect of Plan Termination
nodes.heading: Section 11.2 Effect of Plan Termination .
nodes.start_phrase: If the Plan is terminated, no additional deferrals or contributions shall be credited to any Parti cipant Account hereunder .
nodes.summary:
- Burden of Proof (Sec. 10.6): Claimants asserting benefits based on facts not in the Plan’s records (e.g., service or compensation such as Base Salary, Incentive Pay, RSP/RP-related amounts) must provide satisfactory affirmative evidence. The Administrator has sole discretion to determine whether the evidence is satisfactory.
- Administrator’s Sole Authority (Sec. 10.7): For all matters under Article 10, the Administrator has exclusive authority; the Committee cannot limit or interfere.
- Plan Amendment (Sec. 11.1): The Committee (or delegate) may amend or terminate the Plan, but cannot reduce/modify benefits already being paid and cannot make changes that violate Section 409A. Definitions of Base Salary or Incentive Pay cannot be amended in a way that impermissibly alters existing deferral elections.
- Effect of Plan Termination (Sec. 11.2): Upon termination, no further deferrals or contributions are made; accounts are paid as provided in Article 8. The Committee may distribute existing account balances at or after termination, ending further obligations, but only as permitted by Section 409A.
- General Provisions—Unfunded Status (Sec. 12.1): The Plan is unfunded; no trust or fiduciary relationship is created. Deferrals are part of the Company’s general assets, and participants’/beneficiaries’ rights to payment are unsecured, no greater than those of general creditors.

nodes.title: GENERAL PROVISIONS
nodes.heading: ARTICLE 12 GENERAL PROVISIONS
nodes.start_phrase: Nothing in the Plan shall create, or be construed to create, a trust of any kind or fiduciary relationship between the Company and the Participant, his or her designated Beneficiary , or any other person.
nodes.summary:
- Burden of Proof (Sec. 10.6): Claimants must provide satisfactory affirmative evidence for any facts not in the Plan’s records, including claims based on unrecorded service or compensation (e.g., Base Salary, Incentive Pay, RSP-/RP-Related Account purposes). The Administrator has sole discretion to decide if the evidence is satisfactory.
- Administrator’s Sole Authority (Sec. 10.7): For all matters under Article 10, the Administrator has exclusive authority; the Committee has no authority and may not limit or interfere.
- Amendments and Termination (Article 11):
  - Plan Amendment (Sec. 11.1): The Committee or its delegate may amend or terminate the Plan, but cannot reduce or modify benefits already payable to Participants or Beneficiaries receiving payments at the time. All amendments must comply with Section 409A; definitions of Base Salary and Incentive Pay cannot be changed in a way that impermissibly alters existing deferral elections.
  - Effect of Plan Termination (Sec. 11.2): Upon termination, no further deferrals/contributions are credited. Accounts are paid as provided in Article 8. The Committee may distribute existing account balances at termination or later, with no further obligations after distribution, all subject to Section 409A.
- General Provisions (Article 12):
  - Unfunded Status (Sec. 12.1): The Plan creates no trust or fiduciary relationship; deferred amounts remain part of the Company’s general funds, and rights to payment are limited accordingly.

nodes.title: Unfunded Status
nodes.heading: Section 12.1 Unfunded Status .
nodes.start_phrase: Nothing in the Plan shall create, or be construed to create, a trust of any kind or fiduciary relationship between the Company and the Participant, his or her designated Beneficiary , or any other person.
nodes.summary:
- Burden of Proof: Claimants seeking benefits based on facts not in the Plan’s records must provide satisfactory affirmative evidence; the Administrator has sole discretion to determine if the evidence is sufficient.
- Administrator’s Exclusive Authority (Article 10): The Administrator alone controls matters under Article 10; the Committee has no authority to limit or interfere.
- Plan Amendments and Termination (Article 11):
  - The Committee (or delegate) may amend or terminate the Plan but cannot reduce benefits already being paid to Participants or Beneficiaries.
  - Amendments must comply with Section 409A; definitions of Base Salary and Incentive Pay cannot be changed in a way that impermissibly alters existing deferral elections.
  - Upon termination, no further deferrals/contributions; accounts are paid per Article 8. The Committee may distribute account balances upon or after termination, only as permitted by Section 409A.
- Unfunded Status (Article 12): The Plan is unfunded; participants are unsecured general creditors. No trust or fiduciary relationship is created, though the Company may hedge obligations.
- Non-Transferability: Rights to deferred compensation cannot be assigned or pledged, except by laws of descent and distribution.
- No Right to Continued Employment: Participation does not guarantee continued employment; the Company may terminate employment without liability under the Plan.
- Plan Benefits and Other Employee Plans: Deferred compensation under this Plan is not treated as compensation for other benefit plans unless those plans expressly provide otherwise.
- Section 409A Compliance: The Plan is intended to comply with Section 409A and will be interpreted and operated accordingly. If necessary, it may be operated in compliance pending amendment while adhering as closely as possible to existing terms.
- No Tax Guarantees: The Company and related parties make no representations or guarantees regarding tax consequences of deferrals or payments. Payments made per Plan terms and beneficiary designations are binding and release the Company and its personnel from related claims.

nodes.title: Non-Transferable
nodes.heading: Section 12.2 Non-Transferable .
nodes.start_phrase: The right of any Participant, or other person, to the payment of deferred compensation under the Plan shall not be assigned, transferred, pledged or encumbered except by the laws of descent and distribution.
nodes.summary:
- Plan obligations are unsecured; participants are general creditors. The Company may, but is not required to, hedge its obligations.
- Participants’ rights to deferred compensation are non-transferable, except by laws of descent and distribution.
- Participation does not guarantee continued employment; the Company may terminate employment at any time without liability under the plan.
- Deferred amounts are not treated as salary/compensation for other benefit plans unless those plans expressly provide otherwise.
- The plan is intended to comply with Internal Revenue Code Section 409A and will be interpreted and administered to maintain compliance; if needed, it may be operated in compliance pending amendment while adhering as closely as possible to existing terms.
- The Company provides no guarantees or representations regarding tax consequences (federal, state, local, income, estate, or gift) for participants or beneficiaries.
- Payments made according to plan terms and beneficiary designations are binding on all parties and discharge the Company and its representatives from related claims.

nodes.title: No Right to Continued Employment
nodes.heading: Section 12.3 No Right to Continued Employment .
nodes.start_phrase: Participation in the Plan shall not be construed as conferring upon the Participant the right to continue in the employ of the Company as an executiv e or in any other capacity .
nodes.summary:
- Plan benefits are unsecured obligations of the company; participants are general unsecured creditors. The company may, but is not required to, purchase securities or instruments to hedge its obligations.
- Deferred compensation rights are non-transferable and cannot be assigned, pledged, or encumbered, except by laws of descent and distribution.
- Participation does not guarantee continued employment; the company may terminate employment at any time without liability under the plan.
- Deferred compensation is not treated as salary or compensation for purposes of other employee benefit plans unless expressly stated in those plans.
- The plan is intended to comply with IRC Section 409A and will be interpreted, administered, and, if necessary, operated and amended to maintain compliance while adhering as closely as possible to existing terms.
- The company makes no guarantees regarding tax consequences. Payments made in accordance with the plan and beneficiary designations are binding on all parties and release the company and its representatives from related claims; no representations are made about federal, state, or local tax treatment for participants or beneficiaries.

nodes.title: Plan Benefits Not Compensation Under Employee Benefit Plans
nodes.heading: Section 12.4 Plan Benefits Not Compensation Under Employee Benefit Plans .
nodes.start_phrase: Any deferred compensation payable under the Plan shall not be deemed salary or other compensation to the Particip ant for the purpose of computing the benefits under any plan or arrangement (including but not limited to any “employee benefit plan” under ERISA) except as expressly provided in such plan or arrangement.
nodes.summary:
- Participants’ deferred compensation rights are unsecured; they have the status of general unsecured creditors. The Company may, but is not required to, purchase securities or other instruments to hedge its obligations.
- Benefits under the Plan are non-transferable and cannot be assigned, pledged, or encumbered, except by laws of descent and distribution.
- Participation does not confer any right to continued employment; the Company may terminate employment at any time without liability related to Plan participation.
- Deferred compensation paid under the Plan is not treated as salary or compensation for purposes of other employee benefit plans unless such plans expressly provide otherwise.
- The Plan is intended to comply with Internal Revenue Code Section 409A and will be interpreted and administered accordingly; if needed, it may be operated in compliance pending formal amendments, adhering as closely as possible to existing terms while meeting 409A requirements.
- The Company disclaims any guarantees regarding tax consequences for participants or beneficiaries. Payments made in accordance with Plan terms and beneficiary designations are binding and release the Company and related parties from claims. No person associated with the Plan guarantees any specific federal, state, or local tax treatment of deferrals or payments.

nodes.title: Compliance with Section 409A
nodes.heading: Section 12.5 Compliance with Sectio n 409A .
nodes.start_phrase: The Plan is intended to comply with Section 409A, and shall be interpreted, operated and administered consistent with this intent and the Section 409A Policy.
nodes.summary:
- Plan obligations to participants are unsecured; the company may, but is not required to, hedge these obligations.
- Deferred compensation rights are non-transferable, except by laws of descent and distribution.
- Participation does not confer any right to continued employment; the company may terminate employment at any time without liability under the plan.
- Deferred compensation is not treated as salary or compensation for other employee benefit plans unless explicitly stated in those plans.
- The plan is intended to comply with Internal Revenue Code Section 409A and will be interpreted, administered, and, if necessary, temporarily operated and amended to maintain compliance.
- The company and related parties do not guarantee any tax outcomes for participants or beneficiaries; payments made according to the plan and beneficiary designations are binding and release the company from related claims.

nodes.title: No Guarantee of Tax Consequences
nodes.heading: Section 12.6 No Guarantee of Tax Consequences .
nodes.start_phrase: (a) The Company makes no represent ations or warranties and assumes no responsibility as to the tax consequences to any Participant who enters into a deferred compensation agreement with the Company pursuant to the Plan or any such Participant’ s Beneficiary .
nodes.summary:
- Plan obligations are unfunded and unsecured; participants have the status of general unsecured creditors. The Company may, but is not required to, hedge its obligations with securities or other instruments.
- Deferred compensation rights are non-transferable except by laws of descent and distribution.
- Participation does not guarantee continued employment; the Company may terminate employment at any time without liability under the Plan.
- Plan benefits are not treated as salary or compensation for other employee benefit plans unless expressly provided.
- The Plan is intended to comply with IRC Section 409A and will be interpreted, operated, and, if necessary, amended to maintain compliance while adhering as closely as possible to existing terms.
- No guarantee of tax consequences: the Company makes no representations regarding federal, state, or local tax treatment (including income, estate, and gift taxes); payments made per Plan terms are binding and release related claims; this disclaimer is incorporated into all Plan agreements.
- Limitations on liability: no additional legal or equitable rights beyond the Plan and law; no guarantee against loss or depreciation of accounts; the Company and its affiliates are not liable for investment losses or tax outcomes, with the obligation limited to making payments per the Plan.
- Severability: invalid provisions do not affect the remainder of the Plan.
- Captions are for convenience and not part of the Plan’s construction.
- Governing law: New York law applies, subject to federal law, without regard to conflict-of-laws principles.

nodes.title: Limitations on Liability
nodes.heading: Section 12.7 Limitations on Liability .
nodes.start_phrase: Neither the establis hment of the Plan nor any modification thereof, nor the creation of any account unde r the Plan, nor the payment of any benefits under the Plan shall be construed as giving to any Participant or other person any legal or equitable right against the Company , or any officer or employer thereof except as provided by law or by any Plan provision.
nodes.summary:
- Section 12.6 incorporation: Any agreement executed under the Plan is deemed to include the provision(s) of Section 12.6.
- Section 12.7 Limitations on Liability: The Plan and related actions do not create rights beyond those in law or the Plan; account values are not guaranteed against loss (including investment performance or insolvency); the Company and its stakeholders are not liable for claims arising from the Plan or its implementing instruments or for tax outcomes, except the Company’s obligation to pay benefits as specified.
- Section 12.8 Severability: Invalid or illegal provisions do not affect the rest of the Plan, which remains enforceable without them.
- Section 12.9 Captions: Headings are for convenience only and not part of the Plan’s interpretive text.
- Section 12.10 Governing Law: The Plan is governed by New York law to the extent not superseded by federal law, without applying conflict-of-law principles.

nodes.title: Severability
nodes.heading: Section 12.8 Severability .
nodes.start_phrase: If any provision of the Plan is held to be illegal or void, such illegality or invalidity shall not affect the remaining provisions of the Plan, but shall be fully severable, and the Plan shall be construed and enforced as if said illegal or invalid provision had never been inserted herein.
nodes.summary:
- Any agreement made under the Plan automatically incorporates the referenced provision of Section 12.6.
- Limitations on liability: establishing or modifying the Plan, creating accounts, or paying benefits does not create rights beyond the Plan and law; no guarantees against investment losses or insolvency-related losses; the Company and its affiliates/individuals are not liable for claims arising from the Plan or its implementing instruments, except to make benefit payments as provided; no assurance of any particular tax outcomes.
- Severability: if any provision is illegal or invalid, it is severed and the rest of the Plan remains enforceable.
- Captions: headings are for convenience only and do not affect interpretation.
- Governing law: the Plan is governed by New York law to the extent not superseded by federal law, without applying conflict-of-laws principles.

nodes.title: Captions
nodes.heading: Section 12.9 Captions .
nodes.start_phrase: The headings and captions herein are provided for reference and convenienc e only, shall not be considered part of the Plan, and shall not be considered in the construction of the Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Agreements executed under the Plan automatically incorporate the provisions of Section 12.6.
- Limitations on liability: the Plan’s existence, modifications, accounts, or benefit payments do not create rights beyond those in the Plan or law; neither the Company nor its affiliates or personnel guarantee account values or investment performance (including losses from insolvency), and are not liable for claims related to the Plan or its implementing instruments, except to make benefit payments as specified; no assurance is given regarding tax consequences.
- Severability: any illegal or invalid provision is severed without affecting the remainder of the Plan.
- Captions: headings are for convenience only and have no interpretive effect.
- Governing law: the Plan is governed by New York law, subject to federal preemption, without applying conflict-of-law principles.

nodes.title: Governing Law
nodes.heading: Section 12.10 Governing Law .
nodes.start_phrase: The Plan shall be construed in accorda nce with and governed by the laws of the State of New York to the extent not superseded by federal law , without reference to the principles of conflict of laws.
nodes.summary:
- States that any agreement executed under the Plan is deemed to include the referenced provision of Section 12.6.
- Limits liability: establishing or modifying the Plan, creating accounts, or paying benefits does not grant rights beyond the Plan or law; neither the Company nor its personnel guarantee account values or are liable for losses, investment performance, insolvency-related losses, plan-related claims, or unintended tax outcomes, except for the Company’s obligation to pay benefits per the Plan.
- Includes a severability clause ensuring invalid provisions do not affect the remainder of the Plan.
- Clarifies that headings/captions are for convenience only and not part of the Plan’s construction.
- Sets governing law as New York law (subject to federal preemption and excluding conflict-of-laws principles).
